docs.title: Disconnect Unused Interfaces
docs.text: If a communication interface is not used by the application, disconnect its communication cable. For example, an application using only digital I/O does not need a permanently connected communication interface used only for parameterization.

docs.title: Close Unused Ports and Services
docs.text: Disable every protocol that is not required for operation. This reduces the device's attack surface.

docs.title: Legacy Protocols (CoLa)
docs.text: CoLa1 (CoLa ASCII/Binary) is a legacy interface for configuration and status requests. Disable it when the application does not need it. On multiScan200 and picoScan100, manage this service under Diagnostics > Cybersecurity; CoLa1 is disabled by default on multiScan200 and enabled by default on picoScan100. On LRS4000 and multiScan100, inspect the service state and available controls on the device before changing it.

docs.title: SOPAS ET Device Search
docs.text:
Limit device visibility through broadcast scanning. On picoScan100, the device search setting offers four modes:

SOPAS ET Device Search: mode and behavior.

Mode Behavior Enabled The device can be discovered and its IP address can be changed without authentication. Time-Limited The device can be discovered and its IP address can be changed without authentication for 60 seconds after boot. Restricted The device can be discovered, but its IP address cannot be edited without authentication. Disabled The device cannot be discovered. Recommended where applicable.

Device search uses UDP port 30718. It is Time-Limited by default on the picoScan100.

On the multiScan200, device search is enabled by default; disable it in Diagnostics > Cybersecurity when it is not required.

On LRS4000 and multiScan100, check the device's cybersecurity service list for the device-search service and its current state. The picoScan100 modes and default values above do not necessarily apply to those families.

docs.title: Web Server
docs.text: On multiScan200 and picoScan100, the web server uses TCP port 80 and is enabled by default. It provides browser-based visualization and parameterization; when disabled, the sensor remains reachable through SOPAS ET. For LRS4000 and multiScan100, inspect the cybersecurity service list before disabling web access.

docs.title: CoLa2
docs.text: CoLa2 uses TCP port 2122. On picoScan100 it cannot be disabled. On multiScan200 it is disabled by default; enable it in Diagnostics > Cybersecurity only when required. Check the product-specific service list for CoLa2 availability on other families.

docs.title: Measurement Data Output
docs.text:
Enable measurement data output only when required:

  1. Log in as Authorized client.
  2. Open Application > Data output > Measurement data output.
  3. Enable UDP streaming.

Enabling measurement data output opens a device-side UDP port. Disabling it closes that port again.

docs.title: IMU Data Output
docs.text: Where supported by the device variant and licenses, configure IMU output under Application > Data output > IMU data output as Authorized client. Enable UDP streaming only when required. It opens a device-side UDP port; disabling the stream closes the port.

docs.title: Digital I/O
docs.text: Configure digital signals for device-specific application signals, such as DeviceNotReady or field evaluations, under Configuration > Inputs and outputs. Log in as Authorized client.

docs.title: Date and System Time
docs.text: Configure synchronized time under Basic settings > Date and system time as Authorized client, where this setting is available. NTP uses network time-server traffic. All four families support PTP over UDP ports 319 and 320. Check the device's service list and time-synchronization guide for supported methods and current state.

docs.title: User Levels
docs.text: On all devices, only Service is enabled in the factory state; it cannot be deactivated. See User Levels.

docs.title: Use Encrypted Communication
docs.text: Use HTTPS to encrypt web-interface and REST communication. Measurement data sent over UDP or TCP is not encrypted by HTTPS. Follow the HTTPS & certificates guide to upload a valid certificate bundle and verify the enabled state.

docs.title: Advanced Protection
docs.text: Advanced settings are applied in addition to the basic settings.

docs.title: Limit Network Access by IP Range
docs.text:
Change the default IP address to a non-default value and limit the subnet mask to the smallest subnet that meets the application's needs. Subnetting reduces broadcast traffic and makes it easier to isolate network problems.

Configure this under Configuration > Connection options > Ethernet as Service.

docs.title: Primary Sensor Data
docs.text: The supported data formats vary by family. Use the Data Streaming overview to choose a format available on the device and review its security implications. Measurement data sent over UDP or TCP is not encrypted by HTTPS. The notes below on telegram fields are limited to the named formats and families.

docs.title: Compact Format (Recommended)
docs.text:
Compact packets contain user data and a CRC32 checksum. Telegram headers and fields differ by format and family.

Type 1 scan telegrams are used by LRS4000, multiScan100, and picoScan100.

multiScan200 uses type 6 scan telegrams.

Consult the Compact format guide for the device-specific fields used to check data identity, ordering, timing, and integrity.

docs.title: MSGPACK Format (multiScan100 and picoScan100)
docs.text:
MSGPACK is available on multiScan100 and picoScan100. The following packet fields and segment details describe the documented picoScan100 structure; check the matching product documentation before relying on them for another family.

MSGPACK Format (multiScan100 and picoScan100): field and purpose.

Field Purpose Telegram counter Counts measurement-data telegrams since power-up, starting at 1; detects lost data. Transmit timestamp Sensor system time in microseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC; detects delays. Synchronize the sensor with a time server where required. Segment counter Identifies segments. A 276° frame is split into 10 segments of 30° or 5 segments of 60°, depending on the scanning frequency. Frame number Counts frames since device startup; detects lost data. Sender ID Contains the device serial number; identifies the sending sensor. CRC32 checksum Follows the user data and is calculated over the MSGPACK buffer only, without the STX bytes and the size field.

docs.title: LMDscandata Format (LRS4000 and picoScan100)
docs.text:
LMDscandata is available on LRS4000 and picoScan100. The following field details describe the documented picoScan100 structure; check the product-specific telegram listing for another family:

LMDscandata Format (LRS4000 and picoScan100): field and purpose.

Field Purpose Serial number Identifies the sending device. Telegram counter Counts telegrams created since power-up, starting at 1; detects lost data. Version number Identifies the serialization version and helps trace structure changes. Scan counter Counts scans actually created by the device. Time since startup Counts microseconds since power-up, starting at 0. Device time Sensor system time since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC in microseconds; detects delays. XOR checksum Verifies transfer integrity. CoLa B only: one byte, the XOR of all data bytes.

docs.title: Secondary Sensor Data
docs.text:
multiScan100 and picoScan100 use Compact type 2 for IMU data. multiScan200 uses type 7, with its standard header. The LRS4000 provides IMU data through CoLa events or the REST API instead of Compact. Use the Compact format guide for device-specific IMU fields:

  • Telegram version: the described telegram structure uses version 1.
  • IMU sensor timestamp: sensor system time in µs since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC; detects delays in the data stream.
  • CRC32 checksum: CRC32 of all words except the checksum.

docs.title: Device State
docs.text:
Monitor device state to detect changes in parameterization:

  • CoLa sRN SCdevicestate transmits the general device state.
  • REST GET /api/DeviceStatus reads the device status.

docs.title: Last Modified Information
docs.text: Protect and monitor the information about when device parameters were changed and stored. Find it under Diagnosis > Overview > Operating information.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text: Regularly review the diagnostic overview under Diagnosis > Overview > Messages. If the sensor is not working as intended, use the troubleshooting information to correct the problem or determine how to proceed.

docs.title: Diagnostic File
docs.text:
The device provides a diagnostic file for in-depth analysis. Only SICK can read this file. Use NTP synchronization so that device information can be assigned correctly:

  1. Log in as Service.
  2. Open Basic settings > Date and system time and configure NTP or PTP.
  3. Open Diagnostics > Overview > Diagnostic file.
  4. Select Create file, then download the file.

docs.title: Changing Parameters
docs.text: Prevent unauthorized operators from changing parameters because parameter changes can alter application results. Limit access to device parameters to the minimum number of people required by the need-to-know principle.

docs.title: Kaitai Struct Parsers
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

Kaitai Struct generates parsing code from a binary-format description. Use SICK's KaitaiStructDescriptions to build a Compact parser in Python, C++, C#, Java, Go, or another supported language instead of implementing the byte layout yourself.

docs.title: What Is Kaitai Struct?
docs.text:
A .ksy file describes a binary format in YAML: field names, data types, byte order, repeated structures, and conditions. The compiler turns that description into parser classes for your chosen language. The same description can therefore serve applications written in different languages without maintaining separate byte-offset logic.

The Web IDE combines a hex view with a parsed field tree. Load a captured telegram to explore the structure before adding the generated code to your application.

docs.title: Compact Frame and Payloads
docs.text:
The definitions are in the repository's formats directory. Start with compact_frame.ksy: it reads the outer frame and selects the payload definition using telegram_type. Keep the other .ksy files alongside it because the frame imports them. The definitions cover scan, IMU, ambient-light, and encoder telegrams; availability depends on the sensor.

All telegrams have the following outer frame. Multi-byte numbers are little-endian.

Compact Frame: fields in transmission order, size, and purpose.

Field Size Purpose start_of_frame 4 bytes Start marker: 02 02 02 02 telegram_type 4 bytes Selects the payload definition payload Variable Scan, IMU, ambient-light, or encoder data checksum 4 bytes CRC32 over the start marker, telegram type, and payload

The frame definition imports these payload definitions:

Payload Definitions: telegram type, content, and supported devices.

Type Definition Devices 1 Scan data, spherical coordinates LRS4000, multiScan100, picoScan100 2 IMU multiScan100, picoScan100 3 Ambient light multiScan200 4 Encoder picoScan150 6 multiScan200 scan data multiScan200 7 IMU with standard header multiScan200

Types 3, 4, 6, and 7 use the shared standard header. Types 1 and 2 have their own layouts. Use the linked definitions for the complete field layout and the operating instructions for device-specific output settings.

docs.title: Generate in the Web IDE
docs.text:
1. Download the repository using Code > Download ZIP and extract it.
  2. Open the Kaitai Web IDE.
  3. Import the .ksy files from formats, including compact_frame.ksy and its dependencies.
  4. Right-click compact_frame.ksy in the file tree, select Generate Parser, and choose your target language.
  5. Save the generated modules and add them to your application together with the matching Kaitai Struct runtime library.

To inspect a capture, load a .bin file containing one complete Compact telegram into the hex view. Use only the application payload, including the Compact start marker and checksum, not a complete Ethernet packet or a PCAP file.

docs.title: Generate from the Command Line
docs.text:
Install the Kaitai Struct compiler, including its Java prerequisite, and add kaitai-struct-compiler to your PATH. Clone the definitions and generate a Python parser:

git clone https://github.com/SICKAG/KaitaiStructDescriptions.git
Set-Location KaitaiStructDescriptions
kaitai-struct-compiler -t python --outdir generated formats\compact_frame.ksy

The compiler writes compact_frame.py and the imported payload modules to generated. Keep those modules together. For another language, change the -t value; run kaitai-struct-compiler --help to list the supported targets.

For example, generate C# or C++/STL code with:

kaitai-struct-compiler -t csharp --outdir generated-csharp formats\compact_frame.ksy
kaitai-struct-compiler -t cpp_stl --outdir generated-cpp formats\compact_frame.ksy

For Python, install the runtime in your application's environment:

python -m pip install kaitaistruct

The runtime reads the binary data; the compiler is needed only when generating or updating the parser. Other target languages need their corresponding runtime library.

Warnings suggesting num_* names for count fields are style warnings, not parsing errors.

docs.title: Use the Generated Parser
docs.text: Pass one complete Compact telegram to the generated CompactFrame parser. Read telegram_type first, then access the corresponding payload fields. See Compact Format for the telegram types, field conventions, and conversion to Cartesian coordinates.

docs.title: Scan Data
docs.text:
For type 1, payload.header contains the telegram version and counter. payload.module holds the modules; each module has metadata and beam data. The metadata describes the number of beams, layers, and echoes, the acquisition times, and the elevation and azimuth angles.

This Python example reads one complete Compact telegram from telegram.bin, for example a UDP payload saved with File > Export Packet Bytes in Wireshark, and prints every echo:

import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "generated")  # folder written by kaitai-struct-compiler
from compact_frame import CompactFrame

with open("telegram.bin", "rb") as file:  # one complete Compact telegram
    frame = CompactFrame.from_bytes(file.read())

if frame.telegram_type == 1:
    for module in frame.payload.module:
        meta = module.metadata
        print("frame", meta.frame_number, "beams", meta.number_of_beams_per_scan)
        for beam in module.beams:
            for line in beam.lines:
                for echo in line.echos:
                    distance = echo.distance if meta.data_content_echos.distance else None
                    rssi = echo.rssi if meta.data_content_echos.rssi else None
                    print(distance, rssi)

Example code: MIT License, © 2026 SICK AG. Provided as is, without warranty. Test it before you use it with a machine or in production.

The generated distance property applies the version-4 scaling factor and returns millimeters. distance_raw is the unscaled value. Check the content flags before accessing optional fields. Combine distance with the layer elevation and beam azimuth for point-cloud reconstruction; see Type 1: Scan Data.

docs.title: IMU Data
docs.text:
Type 2 has a fixed-size payload without repeated scan modules. Its fields are available directly under frame.payload. Which measurements are usable depends on the sensor.

IMU Fields: generated payload fields and their meaning.

Field Meaning acceleration.x, .y, .z Acceleration in m/s² angular_velocity.x, .y, .z Angular velocity in rad/s orientation.w, .x, .y, .z Orientation quaternion timestamp Sensor timestamp in microseconds

For multiScan200, select type 7 instead. It has the standard header before the IMU measurements.

docs.title: Encoder Data
docs.text:
Type 4 links an external encoder reading to the scan through frame_number. The common header is under frame.payload.header; encoder values are directly under frame.payload.

Encoder Fields: generated payload fields and their meaning.

Field Meaning frame_number Identifies the corresponding scan frame tick_count Current encoder count tick_count_at_reference_signal_1, tick_count_at_reference_signal_2 Counts captured at reference signals speed Speed in units/s according to the configured conversion rate tick_count_timestamp Time of the last count change timestamp_of_reference_signal_1, timestamp_of_reference_signal_2 Times of the reference-signal events

For an application example, see 3D With 2D LiDARs.

picoScan100 example: Receive Compact data in C# with Kaitai Struct after reviewing the generated parser. Your application still needs the reception and validation handling described below.

docs.title: Reception and Validation
docs.text:
The parser does not receive data from the sensor. Your application must handle the connection and telegram boundaries:

  • For UDP, receive the complete datagram payload. IP fragments must be reassembled before parsing.
  • For TCP, collect bytes until a complete Compact telegram is available. A single socket read can contain part of a telegram or several telegrams.
  • Validate the CRC32 separately. The frame definition reads the checksum but does not verify it.
  • Handle truncated or unsupported telegrams explicitly. Check the sensor's operating instructions and firmware compatibility before using decoded values.

To compare your decoded values with a capture, use the Compact Wireshark dissector. If you prefer a library that also handles reception, see Coding Tools & Examples.

docs.title: MATLAB Integration
docs.text:
Compatible with: multiScan200 picoScan100

MATLAB ROS Toolbox can subscribe directly to native ROS 2 data from multiScan200 or picoScan100 through DDS. No SICK ROS driver or bridge is required. The example below uses picoScan100 point-cloud data on /cloud/all_points as sensor_msgs/PointCloud2 with the default ROS domain ID 0.

docs.title: Validated Setup
docs.text:
Validated Setup: component and version or setting.

Component Version / setting Operating system Windows 11 MATLAB R2025b with ROS Toolbox ROS 2 / DDS Kilted with CycloneDDS ROS domain ID 0 (device default)

All DDS participants must use the same domain ID as the sensor. Ensure that the sensor's native ROS 2 interface is enabled and that the computer firewall allows DDS traffic. See Native ROS 2 for sensor-side setup.

docs.title: Receive PointCloud2 Data
docs.text:
The following script creates a MATLAB ROS 2 node, lists visible topics, and prints the number of points received on /cloud/all_points.

node = ros2node("/matlab_cloud_counter");

disp("Available ROS 2 topics:");
disp(ros2("topic", "list"));

% Keep the subscriber handle alive until after message reception.
sub = ros2subscriber( ...
    node, ...
    "/cloud/all_points", ...
    "sensor_msgs/PointCloud2", ...
    @onPointCloud); %#ok<NASGU>

disp("Subscribed to /cloud/all_points");

t0 = tic;
while toc(t0) < 10
    pause(0.1);
end

clear sub node
disp("Finished.");

function onPointCloud(msg)
    pointCount = double(msg.width) * double(msg.height);
    fprintf("PointCloud received: %d points\n", pointCount);
end

Example code: MIT License, © 2026 SICK AG. Provided as is, without warranty. Test it before you use it with a machine or in production.

docs.title: Visualize Live Data
docs.text: Open Apps > ROS 2 Data Analyzer, choose Open > Live Network Data, select Live ROS 2 network data, and set the ROS domain ID to 0. Create a PointCloud Visualizer, choose /cloud/all_points, then select Start.

docs.title: Verify Connectivity
docs.text:
Use the ROS 2 CLI independently of MATLAB to verify that DDS data is present:

ros2 topic echo /cloud/all_points

If no data is visible, confirm the native ROS 2 interface configuration, firewall rules, DDS compatibility, and ROS domain ID. On multiScan200 and on picoScan100 from firmware V2.3.1, the sensor domain ID is configurable (rosDomainId); make sure MATLAB uses the same value.

docs.title: Milestone XProtect Camera Plugin
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 picoScan100

Use Milestone XProtect to display camera video beside LiDAR events. Obtain the camera-specific SICK/Milestone package from the applicable download page: LRS4000, multiScan100, or picoScan100. Look under software or integration downloads. If no package is listed, contact SICK support. Confirm that the package supports your XProtect release.

Milestone MIP SDK documentation explains the underlying plug-in deployment model.

docs.title: Model Context
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

When developing an application for a SICK LiDAR sensor, you can clone the relevant documentation or code repository into your project workspace. A local copy gives your coding assistant access to the repository's examples, configuration files, API usage, and implementation details while you work.

Clone the SICK LiDAR Developer Guide repository alongside your application:

git clone https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_lidar_developer_guide.git

Keep the clone up-to-date when you need the latest context:

git -C sick_lidar_developer_guide pull

This repository-based approach provides source context for your development tools. It is not an MCP server and does not expose an MCP tool or service.

docs.title: PLC Integration
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

Use the CoLa command protocol over a TCP/IP socket to receive measurement, field-evaluation, and I/O data from SICK LiDAR sensors on Siemens, Beckhoff, Mitsubishi, or Rockwell PLCs. SICK does not provide maintained PLC function blocks for the product families on this page; implement a small length-prefixed receive routine using the controller's native TCP socket API.

docs.title: Interface and Approach
docs.text:
For PLC applications, use CoLa B on TCP port 2112. Its length-prefixed telegrams are easier to process than CoLa A on port 2111. Open one bidirectional TCP connection from the PLC to the sensor, keep it open, and poll the required values by sending an sRN request and reading the matching sRA response on that same connection.

Interface and Approach: interface, transport, and suitable use.

Interface Transport Suitable use CoLa A / B TCP 2111 / 2112 PLC commands and telegram access Compact / MSGPACK UDP High-rate scan streams to a computer or edge device REST API HTTP(S) 80 / 443 Configuration, diagnostics, and firmware updates

Configure the sensor once through SOPASair: use a fixed IP address reachable from the PLC, configure scan profiles, field-evaluation groups, and I/O, then export a parameter backup. Do not repeatedly configure the sensor from cyclic PLC logic. Enable LMDscandata only when the PLC requires distance data.

docs.title: Polling and CoLa B Framing
docs.text:
The PLC is the client and connects to <device-ip>:2112. Send a request, receive one complete telegram, parse it, and reconnect after an error or timeout.

connect(device_ip, 2112)
loop:
  send(frame("sRN LMDscandata"))
  reply = receive_one_telegram()
  parse(reply)

Every CoLa B telegram has this layout:

Polling and CoLa B Framing: field, size, and value.

Field Size Value Start 4 bytes 02 02 02 02 Length 4 bytes Big-endian payload length Payload N bytes Command type, name, and data Checksum 1 byte XOR of all payload bytes

TCP is a byte stream: a receive operation can return a partial telegram or several telegrams. Buffer incoming bytes; after at least eight bytes are available, validate the start sequence, read the big-endian length, then wait for exactly 8 + length + 1 bytes. Validate the XOR checksum, consume one telegram, and retain any remaining bytes for the next call.

To validate this logic on a PC before porting it to the PLC, use this Python function on the received bytes:

def next_telegram(buffer: bytearray) -> bytes | None:
    header = b"\x02\x02\x02\x02"
    if len(buffer) < len(header):
        return None
    if buffer[:4] != header:
        start = buffer.find(header)
        if start < 0:
            del buffer[:-3]  # preserve a possible partial header
            return None
        del buffer[:start]
    if len(buffer) < 8:
        return None
    length = int.from_bytes(buffer[4:8], "big")
    if len(buffer) < 8 + length + 1:
        return None  # wait for more bytes
    payload, checksum = bytes(buffer[8:8 + length]), buffer[8 + length]
    del buffer[:8 + length + 1]  # keep the remaining bytes for the next call
    xor = 0
    for byte in payload:
        xor ^= byte
    return payload if xor == checksum else None

Example code: MIT License, © 2026 SICK AG. Provided as is, without warranty. Test it before you use it with a machine or in production.

docs.title: Common Telegrams
docs.text:
Common Telegrams: telegram, purpose, and PLC consideration.

Telegram Purpose PLC consideration SCdevicestate Device health Poll slowly and invalidate dependent values when not ready. LMDscandata Distance and optional RSSI data Reduce it below the network MTU where possible. perpendicularDistanceResult Minimum and maximum distance to a field boundary where the device supports perpendicular distance Its value can remain unchanged after the field is clear; gate it with field state. FieldEvaluationResult Free/occupied result for each evaluation group Map each group index to the configured physical zone. LIDinputstate / LIDoutputstate Digital I/O states Use to mirror sensor I/O in the PLC process image.

Request each with sRN <name> and parse the sRA <name> ... response. Confirm the exact payload layout, byte offsets, and data types against the Telegram Listing for the installed firmware.

To keep LMDscandata manageable, use only the required echo, disable RSSI when not needed, restrict the scan angle, and select the coarsest acceptable angular resolution. A small telegram reduces PLC processing load and TCP segmentation.

docs.title: Controller Notes
docs.text:
Controller Notes: controller and TCP mechanism.

Controller TCP mechanism Siemens S7-1500 / S7-1200 Open User Communication: TCON_IP_v4, TSEND_C, and TRCV_C; use variable-length receives. Siemens S7-300 / S7-400 CP module with AG_SEND / AG_RECV and FB54 TCP. Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 Tc2_TcpIp: FB_SocketConnect, FB_SocketSend, and FB_SocketReceive. Mitsubishi GX Works2 / iQ Ethernet socket services: SP_SOCOPEN, SP_SOCSND, SP_SOCRCV, and SP_SOCCLOSE. Rockwell / Allen-Bradley Raw TCP socket object with MSG instructions for connect, write, read, and close.

The transport API differs, but the CoLa B framing and receive-buffer logic are identical for every PLC.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Troubleshooting: symptom, cause, and action.

Symptom Cause Action Connection refused on 2112 Incorrect network settings or CoLa B disabled Verify the sensor IP/subnet and CoLa B configuration. No response Malformed request or wrong telegram name Validate start bytes, length, XOR checksum, and case-sensitive command name. sFA error response Unsupported or unavailable variable Check the CoLa error codes, Telegram Listing, and firmware version. Receive never completes Fixed-size receive or TCP fragmentation Buffer data and use the length field to determine the complete frame. Misaligned data Concatenated frames or unconsumed bytes Consume exactly one frame and retain the buffer remainder. Frozen values Repeated scan or stale perpendicular-distance result Verify scan counter/timestamp and use FieldEvaluationResult to validate the distance.

docs.title: ROS Integration
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

There are two ways to get LiDAR data into ROS 2: the sensor publishes ROS 2 messages itself (native ROS 2), or a driver on the host receives sensor data and publishes the messages (sick_scan_xd). Both deliver standard ROS 2 messages to your nodes. The difference is which product families they cover and where decoding and publishing run.

ROS Integration: integration path and compatible devices.

Integration path Compatible with Native ROS 2 multiScan200, picoScan100 sick_scan_xd LRS4000, multiScan100, picoScan100

The LRS4000 and multiScan100 do not support native ROS 2. Use sick_scan_xd for these families.

ROS 2 with sick_scan_xd The sensor sends data to the sick_scan_xd driver on the host, which publishes to customer ROS nodes 1 to N over DDS. LiDAR sensor Streaming App ROS 2 sick_scan_xd host driver Customer ROS Node 1 Customer ROS Node 2 Customer ROS Node N Native ROS 2 The native ROS 2 publisher on the sensor sends data over DDS directly to customer ROS nodes 1 to N, without a driver. Uses CycloneDDS as the ROS middleware. LiDAR sensor Streaming App ROS 2 Native ROS 2* Customer ROS Node 1 Customer ROS Node 2 Customer ROS Node N Protocol: driver-supported sensor data Protocol: DDS (Data Distribution Service) via UDP/IP * Native ROS 2 uses CycloneDDS as its ROS middleware (RMW).

ROS Integration: option, what it is, advantages, trade-offs, and best fit.

Option What it is Advantages Trade-offs Best fit Native ROS 2 The sensor firmware assembles the scan segments and publishes ROS 2 messages over DDS. No driver on the host; lower host CPU load; hardware timestamps; any number of subscribers and other DDS clients can receive the data directly. Cyclone DDS is the specified middleware; uses more network bandwidth than Compact; no IMU or diagnostics topics; configuration stays outside ROS 2; the picoScan150 needs a license. ROS 2 systems where host CPU matters, for example navigation or SLAM on embedded computers. sick_scan_xd A ROS 2 driver on the host receives data through the driver-supported sensor protocol, assembles the scans, and publishes the messages. Publishes PointCloud2, LaserScan, and IMU messages where supported; decoding is under host-side control; supports recording to rosbag files. Decoding and publishing use host CPU; the driver must be installed and maintained on the host. Applications that need IMU topics, LRS4000 or multiScan100 integration, or host-side control over decoding.

docs.title: Native ROS 2
docs.text:
Compatible with: multiScan200 picoScan100

The product supports native ROS 2 communication via the DDS (Data Distribution Service) protocol. This enables efficient real-time transmission of measured data without additional drivers and with minimum delay time. The data is output directly in ROS 2-compatible formats.

  • Filter settings in the product have a direct effect on the published data.
  • Subscribed topics are published even if no measurement points are available. It is therefore recommended that you only subscribe to required topics.
  • If the static IP address is changed, a restart of the device is required to output the topics correctly.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Verify the ROS 2 with middleware Cyclone DDS is installed. Install the Eclipse Cyclone DDS middleware using the Cyclone DDS installation instructions.
  2. Enable Native ROS 2 (DDS) in the device web interface, open Application → Data output and set Measurement data output format to Native ROS 2 (DDS).

  3. Create a Cyclone DDS configuration file and set NetworkInterfaceAddress to the IP address of the host interface connected to the sensor, here 192.168.0.100. See the Cyclone DDS configuration reference for additional options.

    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<CycloneDDS
  xmlns="https://cdds.io/config"
  xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:schemaLocation="https://cdds.io/config https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eclipse-cyclonedds/cyclonedds/master/etc/cyclonedds.xsd">
  <Domain>
    <General>
      <NetworkInterfaceAddress>192.168.0.100</NetworkInterfaceAddress>
    </General>
  </Domain>
</CycloneDDS>

  4. Start rviz2 and add one of the published topics.

The picoScan150 requires firmware V2.2.1 or later and an activated native ROS 2 license (PICOSCAN RosConnect). picoScan150 PRO versions (part numbers 1134610 and 1142273) are delivered with this license pre-installed. If the license is missing, contact SICK. See LiDAR License Activation for the official activation instructions.

The picoScan120 requires firmware V2.2.1 or later. The latest firmware and update instructions for both devices are available from the SICK firmware download.

picoScan150 native ROS 2 license.

On Windows, DDS discovery requires the sensor adapter to use the Private network profile; see Getting Started.

The ROS 2 domain ID on the host (ROS_DOMAIN_ID) must match the device. The default is 0; it can be changed with rosDomainId (0-232) or in SOPASair (multiScan200; picoScan100 from firmware V2.3.1). DDS/RTPS discovery must be able to reach the sensor interface. Native ROS 2 publishes data only; configure the sensor through the REST API, CoLa, or the web interface.

docs.title: Visualize the Point Cloud
docs.text:
Start rviz2 with the configuration file from Quick Start step 3:

LinuxWindows

Source ROS 2, select Cyclone DDS, set the configuration file, and start rviz2:

. /opt/ros/<distro>/setup.bash  # for example kilted
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
export CYCLONEDDS_URI="file://$HOME/CycloneDDS/my-config.xml"
rviz2

In rviz2, add /cloud/all_points or a scan topic. Set Fixed Frame to world, or to the frame configured on the device.

In a Windows command prompt, source ROS 2, select Cyclone DDS, set the configuration file, and start rviz2:

call C:\dev\ros2_<distro>\local_setup.bat
set RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
set CYCLONEDDS_URI=file://%USERPROFILE%/cyclonedds.xml
rviz2

In rviz2, add /cloud/all_points or a scan topic. Set Fixed Frame to world, or to the frame configured on the device.

docs.title: Limitations and Trade-Offs
docs.text:
Native ROS 2 is a sensor-to-host data publisher, not a complete ROS 2 control interface:

  • No ROS diagnostics topic: Device health and diagnosis are not exposed as a diagnostics topic in the ROS 2 graph. Use the device web interface for diagnosis and troubleshooting. See the SOPASair overview.
  • Configuration stays outside ROS 2: The interface does not expose sensor parameters, services, or actions. Configure scan profiles, field of view, filters, and other device settings through the web interface, REST API, or CoLa; they cannot be set as ROS parameters or from a ROS 2 launch file.
  • Use CycloneDDS: Native ROS 2 is specified for CycloneDDS as the ROS middleware (RMW) on the host. Other RMW implementations and custom DDS environments are not validated. If you use one, test discovery and communication with your device firmware and ROS distribution.
  • Account for network load: Native ROS 2 uses more network bandwidth than Compact over UDP. The device publishes its available ROS topics concurrently, and topics can continue to be published when a scan contains no measurement points. Subscribe only to topics the application needs, monitor network utilization at the selected scan configuration, and consider Compact if bandwidth is constrained.
  • Publisher changes follow firmware releases: The DDS publisher runs in the sensor firmware, rather than a host-side driver. Publisher fixes and feature changes therefore depend on a firmware release.

docs.title: Published Topics
docs.text:
The native publisher exposes these topics simultaneously. All messages carry the hardware PTP timestamp in header.stamp. The rt prefix is the DDS-level name: in ROS 2 tools, rt<namespace>/cloud/all_points appears as <namespace>/cloud/all_points, for example /cloud/all_points.

The multiScan200 and picoScan100 publish the same PointCloud2 and LaserScan topics. The multiScan200 also publishes the ambient_light and imu topics, and a PointCloud2 topic per segment and echo.

PointCloud2 topics

Published Topics: PointCloud2 topic, contents ¹⁾, output frequency, and description.

PointCloud2 topic Contents ¹⁾ Output frequency Description rt<namespace>/cloud/all_points x,y,z,i,p Scan rate Valid scan points of all segments and all echoes rt<namespace>/cloud/all_points_echo0 x,y,z,i,p Scan rate Valid scan points of echo 0 rt<namespace>/cloud/all_points_echo1 x,y,z,i,p Scan rate Valid scan points of echo 1 (only available if multi-echo is configured) rt<namespace>/cloud/all_points_echo2 x,y,z,i,p Scan rate Valid scan points of echo 2 (only available if multi-echo is configured) rt<namespace>/cloud/reflector_points x,y,z,i,p Scan rate Valid scan points that were recognized as reflectors rt<namespace>/cloud/segment[s] x,y,z,i,p Segment frequency Valid scan points of a selected segment s (only available for segments that are available after application of the angle range filter) rt<namespace>/cloud/segment[s]_echo[e] x,y,z,i,p Segment frequency multiScan200 only: valid scan points of echo e in segment s (only available for segments that are available after application of the angle range filter and depending on the configuration of the echo filter)

¹⁾ intensity (i): RSSI with value range: 0.0 ... 1.0; properties (p): Bit mask 0b00000001 indicates whether this measurement point was recognized as a reflection. On the multiScan200, sWN rosPointCloud2Content selects the optional channels RSSI, properties, time offset, and ring (layer index); see the multiScan200 CoLa Telegram Listing.

Additional topics (multiScan200)

Published Topics: topic and content.

Topic Content ambient_light Passive ambient light image, synchronized with the point cloud imu IMU data: acceleration, angular velocity, and orientation

LaserScan / MultiEchoLaserScan topics

Published Topics: LaserScan / MultiEchoLaserScan topic, data format, contents ¹⁾, output frequency, and description.

docs.title: Frame and Position Parameters
docs.text:
Set the frames and the mounting position on the device; Native ROS 2 has no ROS parameters. Use the CoLa telegrams below, the REST endpoint of the same name, or the web interface.

Frame and Position Parameters: parameter, CoLa telegram, and effect.

Parameter CoLa telegram Effect Frame ID sWN rosFrameId header.frame_id of the published messages Parent frame ID sWN rosParentFrameId Parent frame of the sensor transform, for example world Namespace sWN rosNamespace Prepended to all topic names; empty for no namespace Sensor position sWN SensorPosition Mounting position (x, y, z in mm) and orientation (yaw, pitch, roll in 1/10000°), published as a transform on /tf Domain ID sWN rosDomainId ROS 2 domain ID (0-232); must match ROS_DOMAIN_ID on the host

For the telegram structures and examples, see the CoLa Telegram Listings of the multiScan200 and the picoScan100. After changing the static IP address, restart the device so that the topics are published correctly.

docs.title: DDS Capabilities
docs.text:
Native ROS 2 uses Cyclone DDS and is tested with the rmw_cyclonedds_cpp ROS middleware (RMW) implementation. Other RMW implementations can cause incompatibilities, even when they also use DDS. Use Cyclone DDS for the tested setup; validate interoperability before using a different middleware.

Because the device runs a DDS participant in its firmware, it joins the ROS 2 network as a first-class peer:

  • Interoperability: Compatible ROS 2 nodes, MathWorks ROS Toolbox, and custom DDS clients can subscribe directly, subject to middleware compatibility.
  • Multiple subscribers: The sensor publishes once per scan; adding subscribers does not add another device-side publishing step.
  • Per-subscriber QoS: Subscribers can negotiate policies independently, such as BEST_EFFORT for control and RELIABLE for recording.
  • Automatic discovery: RTPS discovery finds subscribers without a broker or static IP table.
  • Hardware timestamps: header.stamp is set at the hardware scan trigger. With PTP synchronization, it aligns with other sensors.

docs.title: sick_scan_xd
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 picoScan100

The sick_scan_xd driver runs as a ROS 1 or ROS 2 node on the host. It receives sensor data, assembles complete scans, and publishes ROS messages. Choose this approach when you need host-side decoding control, IMU data on ROS topics where supported, or integration with a device that has no native publisher. It also supports recording and playback with rosbag .db3 files. To install it, follow Building the driver: ROS 2 on Linux or ROS 2 on Windows in the README. Then start the launch file for your device as described in Running the driver.

docs.title: CPU Load Comparison
docs.text:
Measurements across 11 picoScan150 profiles used 15-50 Hz scan rates, 0.05-1.0° angular resolutions, 100 scans per method, and IEEE 1588 PTP synchronization. Single-echo sensor_msgs/LaserScan data was used for a direct comparison.

CPU Load Comparison: parameter and value.

Parameter Value Host Raspberry Pi 4, ARM Cortex-A72, 4 cores, Ubuntu 22.04 Network Direct Gigabit Ethernet Latency definition Δt = treceive_on_host − header.stamp

Average system CPU load was 8.5% for native ROS 2 and 21.5% for sick_scan_xd, expressed as the percentage of one Raspberry Pi 4 CPU core.

docs.title: API | CoLa Telegrams
docs.text:
This reference lists the CoLa telegrams supported by the multiScan100. Use the command details to build or troubleshoot PLC and other low-level integrations without guessing the telegram structure. For connection setup, framing, and log in, see CoLa Interface.

Each telegram lists its request and response structure, examples, variable types, lengths, and CoLa A and CoLa B byte values.

Every entry uses the same layout, as in the first entry, Log In: a telegram structure table with the variable type, length, and the values in CoLa A and CoLa B, followed by examples that you can copy.

Examples are grouped by protocol, with each telegram representation in a separate code block and its own copy button.

Categories follow the multiScan100 REST API reference where corresponding CoLa telegrams are available. Select a telegram to expand its structure and examples. A direct link to a telegram opens it automatically. The categories organize the reference; availability still depends on the device variant, firmware, and installed software packages.

docs.title: Autostart Measurement [sWN LMPautostartmeas]
docs.text:
This parameter defines whether the scanner will start to rotate directly and measure when powering up or remain in idle mode. Save the changed setting with sMN mEEwriteall; it takes effect at the next power-up cycle.

In case autostart is deactivated, the sensor will remain in idle mode with the laser switched off.

docs.title: Set Time Stamp [sMN LSPsetdatetime]
docs.text:
The data format in the telegram is: +2009{SPC}+7{SPC}+22{SPC}+12{SPC}+0{SPC}+0{SPC}+0.The numbers represent year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond.

If plus is used up-front the data it is interpreted as an integer decimal number, without the plus it's the scanner reads the data as hex format.

The answer is always in ASCII format.

Does only work if NTP- respectively PTP-Client is not active.

There is no real time clock inside the device. When the scanner is switched off and after a reboot, the time has to be set again. Therefore, it is recommended to use a NTP or a PTP setting.

Telegram structure: sMN LSPsetdatetime

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary)
Command type Method String 3 sMN 73 4D 4E
Command Set time stamp String 14 LSPsetdatetime 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65
Year Uint_16 2 +1970d … +2099d (07B2h … 0833h) 07 B2 … 08 33
Month Uint_8 1 +1d … +12d(01h … 0Ch) 01 … 0C
Day Uint_8 1 +1d … +31d(01h … 1Fh) 00 … 1F
Hour Uint_8 1 +0d … +23d(00h … 17h) 00 … 17
Minute Uint_8 1 +0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh) 00 … 3B
Second Uint_8 1 +0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh) 00 … 3B
Microsecond Uint_32 4 +0d … +999999d(00000000h … 000F423Fh) 00 00 00 00 … 00 0F 42 3F

Example: sMN LSPsetdatetime

CoLa A (ASCII)

<STX>sMN{SPC}LSPsetdatetime{SPC}+2026{SPC}+10{SPC}+6{SPC}+9{SPC}+25{SPC}+28{SPC}+0<ETX>

73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 EA 0A 06 09 19 1C 00 00 00 00

docs.title: Data Reduction
Set Angle Range Filter [sWN LFPangleRangeFilter]
docs.text:
The angle range Horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) limits in units of 1/10000 degree.

BeamIncrement = the 'beamIncrement' which is used to subsample the beams within the selected angle range. With a 'beamIncrement' of n only every nth beam from the selected angle range is copied to the output scan, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. If the beamIncrement is zero it is set to one.

docs.title: Object Evaluation
docs.text:
These telegrams read and configure Object Evaluation. Object Evaluation is available from firmware 2.5.0 and requires the 3D Object Detection Advanced package. Create the evaluations in SOPASair; the telegrams then read their state and change their contour, criteria, and group activation.

The Get... and Set... methods require the Authorized Client user level; without a log in, the device answers with sFA 1. The other telegrams need no log in. Changes are applied immediately but are lost on restart unless you save them with sMN mEEwriteall.

docs.title: Set Object Evaluation Configuration [sMN SetObjectEvaluationConfiguration]
docs.text:
This telegram changes the name and the criteria of an existing object evaluation. Write all parameters; read the current configuration first and change only the values you need. The example sets evaluation 1 to moving objects of at least 200 mm width with a speed between 300 mm/s and 15000 mm/s.

Values outside the allowed range are rejected with sFA 30, and a name longer than 20 characters with sFA 7. A minimum that is greater than its maximum, for example for the size or speed, returns error code 2.

docs.title: API | REST | OpenAPI
docs.text:
This page provides the searchable V2.5.0 REST reference and downloadable OpenAPI description for the multiScan100 family. For REST concepts, authentication, and request patterns, see REST API / OpenAPI.

multiScan100_2.5.0.yaml (Download)

Always match the file to your device's actual firmware version. Function availability can vary by variant and installed software package. The ScanDataFormat enum also lists 3 LMDscandata and 4 NativeROS2; the multiScan100 does not support these formats. Use 1 MSGPACK or 2 Compact.

docs.text:
Returns the current IMU data (e.g. acceleration and orientation). The data uses a coordinate system based on DIN 70000. The x-axis lies on the 90-degree beam of the 0-degree layer. The y-axis is perpendicular to the x-axis and lies in the 0-degree layer. The y-values increase in the counterclockwise rotation direction (right-handed system). docs.title: SOPASair Walkthrough
docs.text:
SOPASair is the built-in web interface of the multiScan100 for parameterization, service, and diagnostics. It runs directly on the sensor, so no software installation is needed. Connect the sensor to the same network as your computer and open http://<sensor-ip>/ in a browser. The factory default address is 192.168.0.1.

You can view status and settings without logging in. To change settings, log in with the Authorized Client user level using the user icon in the top bar.

The SOPASair Home dashboard: device status, 3D live view with field evaluation, input and output states, and detection history at a glance.

docs.title: Home
docs.text:
The Home page summarizes the sensor's state. It is a good place to start before you change any settings.

Status shows separate indicators for the device, connection, measurement, field evaluation, and data output. Because each state is reported independently, the sensor can be measuring while no data is sent to an external receiver.

Device and application status indicators.

Device information lists the model, part number, serial number, firmware version, system time, and the time of the last save. Check the firmware version before you use a firmware-specific API example. Click Find device to make the sensor LEDs blink, so you can identify the unit on site.

Device identity and installed firmware version.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The Configuration menu contains the measurement, filter, mounting, network, and I/O settings. For the matching REST parameters, value ranges, and variant-specific limits, see the multiScan100 OpenAPI reference.

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text:
Configuration > Basic settings contains interlaced mode, the status LED, and the measurement state.

Interlaced mode, LED, and measurement settings.

Date and system time shows the device clock and its synchronization source. Apply computer time sets the sensor clock to your computer's time. For network-based time sources, see Time synchronization.

Device clock and time synchronization settings.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
Configuration > Filter combines the fog, echo, particle, and moving-average filters. The echo filter selects all, first, or last echoes, and the moving-average filter sets the averaging depth. See Filter details to choose the right filters for your application.

Fog, echo, particle, and moving-average filters.

docs.title: Mounting
docs.text:
Configuration > Mounting describes how the sensor is installed. Select a preset mounting position or enter the orientation angles and position offsets. Adjust fields to mounting position moves existing fields to match the new mounting, and Accept IMU data takes the orientation from the internal IMU.

Mounting position, orientation, and offsets.

The Inertial measuring unit (IMU) panel shows the current orientation and acceleration. Because the IMU is not calibrated, use its values as a starting point for the mounting orientation, not as a precise measurement.

IMU orientation and acceleration.

docs.title: Contamination Indication
docs.text:
Configuration > Contamination indication monitors the front window for dirt. The sector diagram shows the contamination state per sector, using the color legend below it. You can configure whether a warning or error is output, the sensitivity, the monitored sectors, the handling of blocked sectors, and the response delay. See Contamination indication for the application background.

Contamination status per sector and evaluation settings.

docs.title: Connection Options
docs.text:
Configuration > Connection options contains the Ethernet settings: addressing mode, IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, MAC address, and link speed.

When you click Apply, the new network settings take effect immediately. The browser loses its connection if the sensor moves to an address that your computer cannot reach, so note the new address before applying the change.

Ethernet addressing and link settings.

docs.title: Inputs and Outputs
docs.text:
Configuration > Inputs and outputs assigns each port a name and a direction. For outputs, select the signal source, inversion, logic, and restart behavior. The connector diagram next to each port shows the corresponding pin. The status panels below show the current input and output states, and Reset counters clears the output switching counters.

Port assignments with connector pin diagrams.

docs.title: Application
docs.text: The Application menu contains measurement-data output and field evaluation. Some variants offer additional functions. For example, the multiScan165S with Safe 3D Object Detection adds a ground filter and perpendicular distance measurement as non-safety-related functions.

docs.title: Data Output
docs.text:
Application > Data output selects the measurement-data format, MSGPACK or Compact, and the UDP destination address and port. Start or stop the data stream from the same panel. See Data streaming to choose a receiver and parser.

Output format, UDP destination, and stream control.

IMU data is streamed separately, with its own destination address, port, and start/stop control.

IMU data output.

Data reduction limits the output by scan layer, angular range, and output interval. Range filter removes points outside a cuboid area or a distance window. If layers or points are missing from the received data, check these settings together with the output format.

Scan-layer, angular-range, and interval reduction.

Cuboid-area and distance filters.

docs.title: Field Evaluation
docs.text:
Application > Field evaluation monitors fields for objects and switches outputs when a field is infringed. Each group combines fields, evaluations, and outputs, and has its own activation source. Resource requirements shows how much of the sensor's evaluation capacity is in use, and Detection list shows recent detections.

Evaluation groups with their activation sources.

See Field evaluation for a complete commissioning procedure and API support.

docs.title: Perpendicular Distance Measurement
docs.text:
Where supported by the device variant and software package, perpendicular distance measurement evaluates points within a field relative to a reference line. The results include minimum and maximum perpendicular distances and the positions of the corresponding measuring points.

See Perpendicular Distance Measurement for configuration steps and result interfaces.

docs.title: Object Evaluation
docs.text:
Object Evaluation provides object properties such as size, speed, and direction for decisions based on object criteria rather than only field infringements. It is available from multiScan100 firmware 2.5.0; check the device variant and installed software package for support.

See Object Evaluation for an introduction and application example.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Diagnostics > Overview combines status, device information, operating information, the current device status, and the message log. Expand Operating information to see the number of power-on cycles, the operating hours, and the time of the last parameterization.

Power-on count, operating hours, and last parameterization.

The message table lists current and past events with their status, number, time, description, and counter. Current device status shows only the messages that are still active. If you need support, use Create diagnostic file to collect the device state in one file and send it to SICK. See Contact.

docs.title: Cybersecurity
docs.text:
Diagnostics > Cybersecurity shows the HTTPS certificates and the Services and protocols table. The table lists each service with its purpose and port, so you can enable only the services your integration needs. See HTTPS and certificates for the complete certificate setup.

Services and protocols with their ports.

The service list is specific to the device and firmware shown. For the multiScan165 port reference and the separately configurable measurement-data ports, see the Cybersecurity network-services matrix.

docs.title: Data Recorder
docs.text:
Diagnostics > Data recorder explains how to install the SICK data recorder on your computer and connect it to the sensor. Use the recorder to capture measurement data for later analysis or support cases.

Installation and connection steps for the data recorder.

docs.title: Detection History
docs.text:
Diagnostics > Detection history records field-evaluation detections. Select the evaluations to include, then start the history. The Statistics section counts the detections per evaluation, and the Detection list shows each event with its time stamp. Use Reset detection history to clear the counters.

Detection counts per evaluation.

docs.title: Release Notes
docs.text: This page summarizes firmware changes for the multiScan100 product family from firmware version 2.x.x. Check the release and device variant before updating or using a feature.

docs.title: General Information
docs.text:
• Firmware 2.x.x is the standard firmware for all multiScan100 variants.
  • multiScan100-S has a separate firmware file, which must be requested.
  • A firmware update typically does not affect active parameter settings.
  • Purchased licenses are not affected by firmware upgrades.
  • Reboot the device after activating or deactivating licenses.

docs.title: Update Instructions
docs.text:
multiScan100 firmware can be updated through SOPAS ET, Sentio Creator, or the web UI (SOPASair) with an .spk software package. For the steps, see Firmware Update.

Update via SOPASair.

Firmware updates through SOPASair in a web browser are supported from version 2.4.1. Use the signed .spk.signed package. Start the update from the device menu or from the link on the displayed firmware version.

docs.title: Firmware 2.5.0
docs.text:
Release date: 22 October 2026

Effective from: SN2644xxxx

3D Object Evaluation / 3D Object Tracking.

  • New 3D Object Evaluation functionality using tracked object characteristics.
  • Filtering by stationary or moving objects, object size, speed, direction of movement, and age.
  • A detailed description is available in the online help in SOPASair.
  • Available within the 3D Object Detection Advanced Package.

Firmware 2.5.0: tracked objects and their characteristics in the SOPASair 3D Object Evaluation view.

Optimization of Motor Parameters.

  • Improved motor control for increased robustness and stability.
  • Improved measurement data availability under challenging operating conditions.

GUI.

  • New Dark Mode.
  • Updated GUI for 3D Object Evaluation.
  • Updated error and notification messages.
  • General usability improvements.

Firmware 2.5.0: SOPASair Dark Mode with the 3D Object Evaluation view.

docs.title: Firmware 2.4.4
docs.text:
Release date: 5 May 2026. Firmware 2.4.3 was not released.

New features.

  • Firmware 2.4.4 is available for multiScan165S. The previous firmware for that variant is 2.3.0.
  • Ground Filter and Perpendicular Distance are available as non-safety-related add-ons for multiScan165S with Safe 3D Object Detection (part number 1151596). See the current multiScan165S operating instructions for details.

Optimization.

The FPGA version was updated for production optimization. Firmware 2.4.4 is functionally identical to 2.4.2.

Known issues.

Contamination-indication sectors may not be saved permanently and can be lost after a reboot.

As a workaround, import an appropriate sensor configuration after reboot and verify the sector setup. Use the REST /ContaminationConfig endpoint or the CoLa A/B sWN ContaminationConfig telegram for parameterization.

docs.title: Firmware 2.4.2
docs.text:
Release date: 20 October 2025

New features.

Firmware 2.4.2 adds support for multiScan166. Earlier firmware versions do not support multiScan166.

docs.title: Firmware 2.4.1
docs.text:
Release date: 20 October 2025

New features.

Ground Filter.

The Ground Filter provides upper and lower ground-threshold values. In applications with moving objects, it can reduce false field-evaluation triggers caused by the ground. When configured correctly, it is intended to retain detection of small objects such as forklift tines. The filter can be used indoors and outdoors. It affects both field evaluation and Perpendicular Distance.

Perpendicular Distance.

For an object inside a configured box-shaped field, Perpendicular Distance can output the object's minimum and maximum distance to an axis (X, Y, or Z). Use sRN perpendicularDistanceResult for a one-time request and sEN perpendicularDistanceResult for event-based output.

Firmware update via web GUI.

Firmware can be updated through the web GUI without SOPAS ET, using the signed .spk.signed package.

Parameter import and export.

The firmware adds parameter import and export through the web GUI.

GUI optimization and feature enhancements.

  • The multiScan-S is now shown with a yellow ring in the GUI. Previously, it was not visually distinguishable from other variants.
  • Field contours uploaded by telegram are transferred directly to the web UI.
  • The Cybersecurity overview shows that the Maintenance and Authorized Client user levels are disabled by default. They can be enabled in the GUI after logging in at the Service user level.
  • HTTPS is supported for multiScan100 GUI components.
  • Full-screen mode can be selected by adding ?fullscreen_mode= to the scan view URL.
  • The web update file dialog allows only signed .spk files.
  • The scan-layer filter has a redesigned interface that makes enabled and disabled layers easier to identify. Each layer can be deactivated individually with a click.
  • The distance filter displays minimum- and maximum-distance spheres to show the selected area.
  • An Undo button was added next to Save.
  • The Fullscreen button was moved from the top line next to split view to the device menu.
  • The DHCP fallback mode was changed to Static IP.
  • The GetFieldEvaluationContour telegram was implemented.

Temperature improvements.

The temperature range was extended from +50 °C to +60 °C when the device is mounted with standard bracket 2130373. The device does not shut off when its temperature exceeds the configured limits.

Firmware 2.4.1: usage condition and mission time.

Usage condition Mission time Continuous use at 25 °C 42 years Continuous use rarely above 30 °C 37.5 years 55% of the time up to 30 °C, 35% up to 40 °C, and 10% up to 50 °C 20 years 70% of the time up to 30 °C and 30% up to 50 °C 18 years 80% of the time up to 30 °C and 20% up to 60 °C 13.4 years Continuous use at 50 °C 8 years

When a configured temperature range is exceeded, an output can be switched. Use these telegrams for temperature warnings:

  • Read current device temperature alarm status: sRN temperatureAlarmStatus
  • Set device temperature alarm configuration: sWN temperatureAlarmConfiguration
  • Read device temperature alarm configuration: sRN temperatureAlarmConfiguration

Bug fixes.

  • Harmonized sensor behavior with other LiDAR sensors.
  • Fixed diagnostic dumps not downloading through the GUI.
  • Fixed measurement data sometimes not appearing in the UI after a browser refresh.
  • Fixed an error when creating fields with X/Y extents greater than 100 m.
  • Fixed missing layer selection in the Object Detection scheme.
  • Fixed the queue-overflow error not resetting when streaming was stopped while the error was active.

docs.title: Firmware 2.3.0
docs.text:
Release date: 2 December 2024

New features.

  • High-resolution layers in 3D Object Detection: Choose among 14 one-degree scan layers or either of two high-resolution layers (2D scan layers 6 or 14). A field can be configured multiple times with different sources. multiScan165 does not have high-resolution layers.
  • Detection History: The 3D Object Detection software adds a page for reviewing field-infringement history and logs of current field status.
  • REST firmware update: Firmware updates can be performed using REST.
  • Online Help: Existing help was updated with new content and guidance.
  • I/O application: Adds a warning when I/O ports cannot be created and removes FieldEvaluationAppState from the source list.
  • CoLa1 password handling: ROM passwords were removed; only RAM passwords are permitted.
  • Third-party components: Updated to newer versions.
  • GUI changes: Input configuration is visible when Port 1 is set to Input; the start page can show field evaluation or measurement data; the Field Evaluation Scan GUI can receive scan layers (for multiScan136, both one-degree and high-resolution layers); and the I/O status display was redesigned.

Bug fixes and improvements.

  • IMU errors, including missing data delivery, now generate an error notification.
  • Fixed mounting position not being written when set in the SOPAS ET device window.
  • More than 20 sources can now be connected to a single output. Previously, exceeding 20 sources produced an error.
  • PTP is no longer shown in the selection list when no PTP license is available.
  • Switching between streaming and field-evaluation views is disabled when either required license is missing.
  • System Diagnosis displays the sensor's local time when configured, instead of UTC.
  • Corrected the translation of “No echo” to “Ignore missing echo.”
  • Duplicated evaluations now appear immediately in the GUI without reloading the browser. Previously, duplicated fields were not displayed and could not be deleted.
  • Fixed the maximum-range circle being tilted; it is positioned in the scanner's zero-degree layer.
  • Fixed the preset mounting position not being displayed correctly.
  • The frame count displayed for field-evaluation response time now reflects the scanning frequency correctly. Previously, a 50 ms response time could incorrectly be shown as three frames.
  • Online Help no longer overlaps the settings area.
  • Opening Object Detection and rapidly clicking + no longer produces Access Denied (/api/EvaluationGroupMapping).
  • White points are visible in Echo View.
  • Fixed CoLa 2 reading and writing of Port Configuration and Source List.
  • Fixed deserialization of Compact azimuth angles above pi.
  • Cleaned up different API interfaces.

Known issues.

Hardware.

At startup, the motor may not begin rotating immediately and a Motor Stalled error may appear in the error log. The sensorless motor driver cannot measure the current frequency at startup. It retries its start sequence, which may take up to six seconds; after ten seconds, software resets the driver module.

Firmware.

  • DoDiagnosis increases system load and can adversely affect measurement operation, potentially causing additional errors.
  • While the GUI creates a diagnostic file, the device LED can remain green and the status can show READY even though 3D Object Detection and field evaluation are blocked. Normal operation resumes when file generation is complete.
  • Ports configured as inputs with a 5-pin system plug do not work with Active Low.

Application and UI.

  • In the Upper Z limit field, the cursor can jump vertically when the field is empty; this does not occur when it contains text.
  • Device-name assignment can produce an error.
  • A soft reset triggered through the UI can cause web-server error messages.
  • Creating fields with an X/Y extent greater than 100 m can cause an error and prevent field evaluation from working.
  • The queue-overflow error is not reset when streaming stops while the error is active.
  • Layer selection is missing in the Object Detection scheme.
  • Duplicating evaluations can fail after a group and evaluation are created, one evaluation is duplicated, and the original is deleted. Adding a new evaluation with ID 1 allows duplication again.

docs.title: Firmware 2.2.2
docs.text:
Compatible with: multiScan100; Release date: 19 August 2024

New features.

Licensed 3D Object Detection for multiScan165.

The licensed SensorApp was already available for multiScan136. For multiScan165, it supports collision avoidance and area monitoring, with up to 48 configurable fields. The evaluation uses real elevation angles based on each sensor's production calibration data. It improves evaluation of object position and size for multiScan136 and multiScan165, using all 16 layers for multiScan165.

More simultaneously active fields require more processing and increase system load. Excessive load can cause performance problems or system errors. Deactivating other features, such as the GUI, measurement-data output, and filters, can reduce load and allow more fields to be active.

  • Additional GUI languages were added.
  • An internal recorder can record and play back data on the device; a separate recorder tool is required.
  • sRN FieldEvaluationGroupState reads evaluation-group state: 0 = not configured, 1 = active, 2 = inactive.
  • Online Help was updated.
  • Scan-GUI visualization was optimized, including use of scanner-specific elevation angles.
  • The GUI now warns when an object is too small compared with the layer distance.
  • Support for multiScan165 was added.

Fixes, improvements, and changes.

  • Improved port selection in 3D Object Detection; ports already in use are no longer selectable.
  • Improved resource monitoring in 3D Object Detection. Warnings indicate potential high load and help identify which functions use resources; creating additional fields no longer produces an error message, only warnings.
  • Applied performance optimizations.
  • Improved the GUI structure.
  • Aligned contamination-indication and warning-LED behavior.
  • Improved 3D Object Detection field visualization.
  • Fields can now be duplicated more than four consecutive times, and group deletion works correctly.
  • Applying the current system time now assigns the required internal variables correctly, preventing an incorrect system-time display.
  • Mounting settings are visible without an IMU license.
  • Improved contamination-indication timing and error handling.
  • Field points deleted in the 3D Object Detection table view are now also removed from the graphical view, so both views show the same values.
  • Corrected display of umlauts in the Input/Output window.
  • Reduced the internally blocked 169.254.x.x IP address range.
  • The Reset and maintain communication interface button now performs the reset correctly.
  • System timestamps, including IMU, 3D Object Detection, and scan timestamps, are in UTC.
  • The interval filter now starts at 2.
  • Removed the sensitivity setting from Inputs/Outputs (edge/level).
  • When more than three echoes are measured, the last echo is used instead of the third.
  • An application-state error now changes the device state to error.
  • Queue-overflow errors are shown only when data loss occurs.

Known issues.

  • More than 100 field points can produce a duplicate error message.
  • In Object Detection, quickly clicking + after opening the page can produce Access Denied (/api/EvaluationGroupMapping).
  • Duplicating fields may not work correctly. Press F5 to refresh the browser as a workaround.
  • GUI CPU usage can increase over time. If the GUI freezes, close and reopen the browser.
  • Connecting more than 20 sources to an output produces an error.
  • The change-password dialog may not disappear.
  • An incorrect error message is shown if polygon points exceed 100 m.
  • The queue-overflow error is not reset when streaming stops while the error is active.

Firmware hash.

The published SHA-256 hash for the firmware file is:

110a4eb514b7ec868ecd97f2fc40ec8418dd5e5f56a7e48a099d649e3a84e2b6

Compare a downloaded file's SHA-256 fingerprint with the value published by SICK to check that the file has not been corrupted or manipulated.

Chrome 128 scan-view issue.

During tests with the Chrome 128 beta, measurement data was not displayed in the 2D and 3D SOPASair visualizations. SOPAS ET was not affected. Microsoft Edge was also affected because it uses the same software base.

Workarounds are to update the sensor to the latest firmware, use Firefox, use SOPAS ET, or use Chrome Portable version 127 or earlier. Firmware 2.2.2 contains a fix for this issue.

docs.title: multiScan200
docs.text:
The multiScan200 is a compact 3D LiDAR sensor family with high detection reliability in harsh environments. The first variant is the multiScan270.

Specifications and data sheet on sick.com

multiScan270: up to 192 layers, 45° vertical and 360° horizontal coverage, depending on configuration. Schematic infrared beams in blue; angles are positive upward.

On sick.com, open your device variant's download area for firmware, EPLAN and CAD data, and available NVIDIA Isaac Sim models and Milestone XProtect plug-ins. See Release Notes for firmware changes.

  • Digital inputs
  • Gigabit Ethernet
  • HTTPS
  • NTP
  • PTP

Inputs, onboard processing, and outputs of the multiScan200. Each column is an independent list.

This reference lists the CoLa telegrams supported by the multiScan200. Use the command details to build or troubleshoot PLC and other low-level integrations without guessing the telegram structure.

Examples are grouped by protocol, with each telegram representation in a separate code block and its own copy button.

A direct link to a telegram opens it automatically. The categories organize the reference; availability still depends on the device variant, firmware, and installed software packages.

docs.title: General
Log In [sMN SetAccessMode]
docs.text:
The password hashes of the default passwords are documented in the operating instructions (PDF) of your device. Do not pass them on, and change the passwords during commissioning.

A log in to the device is necessary to change parameters. In most cases, the user level 'Authorized client' is needed. On delivery, only the Service user level is enabled; until a Service user enables Maintenance or Authorized client, the device answers a log in with these levels with sAN SetAccessMode 0 (see User Levels). docs.title: Set Scan Configuration [sMN mCLsetscancfglist]
docs.text:
Select the scan configuration (field of view, scanning frequency, and angular resolution) by its number. Scan configurations 10 to 12 use interlace mode: they achieve a higher angular resolution by combining scans that are shifted to each other. The supported scan configurations are listed in the parameter table below. Read the active scan configuration with sRN PerformanceProfileNumber. To set it, use sWN PerformanceProfileNumber.

docs.text:

Set Particle Filter [sWN particleFilter]
docs.text:
Configure the particle filter. A point is a particle if fewer than the minimum number of neighbors in its 8-connected neighborhood, over all echoes, are within the distance threshold. See Filter Details.

Required user level: Authorized client.

Telegram structure: sWN particleFilter

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary)
Command type Write request String 3 sWN 73 57 4E
Variable name Particle filter String 14 particleFilter 70 61 72 74 69 63 6C 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72
enable If true a detected particle is filtered out (aka distance set to zero) and subsequent echoes are moved up. Otherwise, the point is flagged in the properties channel. Bool_1 1 False:
True:		 0
1		 00
01
minNumberOfNeighbors If a measurement has less points in its 8-connected neighborhood over all echoes within the distance threshold, this measurement is considered as particle. Uint_16 2 Max: 8 +1 00 01
distanceThreshold Distance threshold value. For a given measurement all points in the 8-connected neighborhood over all three echoes are with a distance less than the distanceThreshold are counted. If the result is below the minNumberOfNeighbors, this measurement is considered as particle Uint_16 2 Max: 2000 +500 01 F4

docs.title: Set Angle Range Focus Filter [sWN angleRangeFocusFilter]
docs.text:
Restricts streaming data output to a specified 3D field of view. The theta parameters define the azimuth range and the phi parameters define the elevation range. Beams outside these ranges are not transmitted. Within the selected range, subsampling can be applied to reduce data bandwidth. Additionally, a focus region can be defined where full resolution is preserved (no subsampling). This filter only affects raw data streaming and has no effect on object detection.

Required user level: Authorized client.

Telegram structure: sWN angleRangeFocusFilter

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary)
Command type Write request String 3 sWN 73 57 4E
Variable name Restricts streaming data output to a specified 3D field of view. The theta parameters define the azimuth range and the phi parameters define the elevation range. Beams outside these ranges are not transmitted. Within the selected range, subsampling can be applied to reduce data bandwidth. Additionally, a focus region can be defined where full resolution is preserved (no subsampling). This filter only affects raw data streaming and has no effect on object detection. 01

phiStart Lower boundary of the elevation range. Layers outside this range are not transmitted. Int_32 4 -250000 FF FC 2F 70
phiStop Upper boundary of the elevation range. Layers outside this range are not transmitted. Int_32 4 +250000 00 03 D0 90
thetaIndexIncrement The 'thetaIndexIncrement' is used to sub-sample the slots within the selected theta angle range. With a 'thetaIndexIncrement' of n only every n'th slot from the selected angle range is serialized, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. Uint_16 2 +1 00 01
phiIndexIncrement The 'phiIndexIncrement' is used to sub-sample the layers within the selected phi angle range. With a 'phiIndex-Increment' of n only every n'th layer from the selected angle range is serialized, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. Uint_16 2 +1 00 01

The telegram is intended to read the current configuration state of the field evaluation. Depending on the device, computational limits can be reached. docs.title: Read Field Evaluation Result [sRN FieldEvaluationResult]
docs.text:
This telegram returns the status information of all evaluations. Possible status codes:

  • Not configured - This evaluation has not been configured.
  • Inactive - This evaluation has been configured but is currently not evaluated.
  • Free - The field is not infringed.
  • Infringed - The field is infringed.
  • Detecting infringed - An infringement has been detected in the field but the response time has not been reached yet.
  • Detecting free - The field is no longer infringed but the time for the free state has not been reached yet.
