docs.title: Error Codes [sFA]
docs.text:
If the device cannot execute a telegram, it answers with sFA and an error code, for example sFA 3 (CoLa A) or 73 46 41 00 03 (CoLa B payload) for an unknown variable name.

Error code Description Dec. Hex. Sopas_Ok No error 0 0 Sopas_Error_METHODIN_ACCESSDENIED Wrong userlevel, access to method not allowed 1 1 Sopas_Error_METHODIN_UNKNOWNINDEX Trying to access a method with an unknown Sopas index 2 2 Sopas_Error_VARIABLE_UNKNOWNINDEX Trying to access a variable with an unknown Sopas index 3 3 Sopas_Error_LOCALCONDITIONFAILED Local condition violated, e.g. giving a value that exceeds the minimum or maximum allowed value for this variable 4 4 Sopas_Error_INVALID_DATA Invalid data given for variable, this errorcode is deprecated (is not used anymore). 5 5 Sopas_Error_UNKNOWN_ERROR An error with unknown reason occurred, this errorcode is deprecated. 6 6 Sopas_Error_BUFFER_OVERFLOW The communication buffer was too small for the amount of data that should be serialised. 7 7 Sopas_Error_BUFFER_UNDERFLOW More data was expected, the allocated buffer could not be filled. 8 8 Sopas_Error_ERROR_UNKNOWN_TYPE The variable that shall be serialised has an unknown type. This can only happen when there are variables in the firmware of the device that do not exist in the released description of the device. This should never happen. 9 9 Sopas_Error_VARIABLE_WRITE_ACCESSDENIED It is not allowed to write values to this variable. Probably the variable is defined as read-only. 10 A Sopas_Error_UNKNOWN_CMD_FOR_NAMESERVER When using names instead of indices, a command was issued that the nameserver does not understand. 11 B Sopas_Error_UNKNOWN_COLA_COMMAND The CoLa protocol specification does not define the given command, command is unknown. 12 C Sopas_Error_METHODIN_SERVER_BUSY It is not possible to issue more than one command at a time to an SRT device. 13 D Sopas_Error_FLEX_OUTOF_BOUNDS An array was accessed over its maximum length. 14 E Sopas_Error_EVENTREG_UNKNOWNINDEX The event you wanted to register for does not exist, the index is unknown. 15 F Sopas_Error_COLA_A_VALUE_OVERFLOW The value does not fit into the value field, it is too large. 16 10 Sopas_Error_COLA_A_INVALIDCHARACTER Character is unknown, probably not alphanumeric. 17 11 Sopas_Error_OSAI_NO_MESSAGE Only when using SRTOS in the firmware and distributed variables this error can occur. It is an indication that no operating system message could be created. This happens when trying to GET a variable. 18 12 Sopas_Error_OSAI_NO_ANSWER_MESSAGE This is the same as Sopas_Error_OSAI_NO_MESSAGE with the difference that it is thrown when trying to PUT a variable. 19 13 Sopas_Error_INTERNAL Internal error in the firmware, probably a pointer to a parameter was null. 20 14 Sopas_Error_HubAddressCorrupted The Sopas Hubaddress is either too short or too long. 21 15 Sopas_Error_HubAddressDecoding The Sopas Hubaddress is invalid, it can not be decoded (Syntax). 22 16 Sopas_Error_HubAddressAddressExceeded Too many hubs in the address 23 17 Sopas_Error_HubAddressBlankExpected When parsing a HubAddress an expected blank was not found. The HubAddress is not valid. 24 18 - An asynchronous method call was made although the device was built with “AsyncMethodsSuppressed”. This is an internal error that should never happen in a released device. 25 19 - Device was built with „ComplexArraysSuppressed“ because the compiler does not allow recursions. But now a complex array was found. This is an internal error that should never happen in a released device. 26 1A

docs.text:
Returns the current IMU data (e.g. Acceleration, Orientation, ... ). The data is given in the following coordinate system which is based on the DIN70000 system. The x-axis lies on the 90-degree-beam of the 0-degree-layer. The y-axis is perpendicular to the x-axis and lies in the 0-degree-layer. The y-values are rising in the counterclockwise rotation direction (right-handed system). The z-axis is perpendicular to the x-y-plane and the scanner top points to rising z-values.

docs.title: SOPASair Walkthrough
docs.text: This page describes the multiScan200 web interface and the settings in each view. Use it to commission the sensor before you automate the configuration through the API. To try the interface without a device, open it in the Virtual Sensor Lab.

docs.title: Home
docs.text:
The Home page gives you the current device status, network identity, firmware version, and an overview of the sensor's operating state. It is usually the first screen you see after logging in and is the quickest place to confirm that the unit is online and healthy before you start changing configuration or application settings.

Home page overview on a live multiScan270 device.

The status bar at the top shows the LED indicator, the device connection status and the measurement status. The toolbar next to it holds Save permanently, the login panel, the language switch and the global help (?). The help includes a Getting started tour that walks through the most important commissioning steps.

Changes take effect immediately but are held in volatile memory. Click Save permanently in the toolbar to store the parameter set in the device and in the cloning memory of the system plug. Unsaved changes are lost at the next power cycle.

For a monitoring display without configuration access, open http://192.168.0.1/#/?fullscreen=.

Status tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

Device information tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

Status of inputs tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

Status of outputs tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

Detection history statistics tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

The LED indicator mirrors the four status LEDs on the housing. LED1 and LED3 show the same colour, as do LED2 and LED4.

Status LED combinations and their meanings on the multiScan270.

LED1/LED3 LED2/LED4 Meaning Red Red Booting, parameterising or firmware update – – Off Red, flashing fast Red, flashing fast Fatal error Red, flashing slowly Red, flashing slowly Recoverable error Green Green Ready, no object detected in configured fields – Green Ready, no fields configured Red Yellow Standby / power saving Green Yellow, flashing Warning Yellow Green, flashing Restart after time or digital input Green Yellow, flashing Contamination warning Red, flashing Yellow, flashing Contamination error Green, flashing Red, flashing Alignment mode Green, yellow, red Green, yellow, red Identify device (Find device) Red Red and yellow, flashing Teach-in environment Yellow Green Object detected

illuminated · flashing · – off

The LEDs are only an additional visual aid. Switching them off in the web interface does not affect diagnostics over Ethernet or the digital I/Os.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Choose the scan configuration and the core measurement behaviour. Resolution, frequency, and range trade off against each other.

The live scan on the left updates as you change the configuration, which is the quickest way to judge a setting.

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text:
Basic Settings controls the scan configuration used by the sensor. The settings are shown on the right; the live scan on the left shows the effect of the selected frequency, angular resolution, and other settings immediately. Use this view to check coverage and measurement behaviour while commissioning.

Basic settings tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

The multiScan270 offers the following scan configurations. The vertical field of view is always 45° (about +22.5° to −22.5°). Configurations 10 to 12 reach their horizontal resolution in interlaced mode, where consecutive scans are offset in angle and combined. The ambient-light image is passively captured by the same receiver used for LiDAR, synchronized with the laser measurement, and has the same scan frequency and horizontal resolution as the configured laser measurement.

multiScan270 scan configurations, angular resolutions, layer counts, ambient-image dimensions, and scan frequencies.

No. Use case FoV (H) Resolution (H × V) Layers Ambient image (pixels, columns × rows) Frequency 1 Default 276° 0.47° × 0.47° 96 592 × 96 20 Hz 2 Less bandwidth, more range 276° 0.47° × 0.94° 48 592 × 48 20 Hz 3 Highest vertical resolution 276° 0.47° × 0.23° 192 592 × 192 20 Hz 4 Full 360° view 360° 0.47° × 0.47° 96 773 × 96 10 Hz 10 High horizontal resolution 276° 0.23° × 0.47° 96 1184 × 96 20 Hz, 2× interlaced 11 High H and V resolution 276° 0.23° × 0.23° 192 1184 × 192 20 Hz, 2× interlaced 12 Highest H and V resolution 276° 0.12° × 0.23° 192 2369 × 192 20 Hz, 4× interlaced 20 Up to +55 °C 190° 0.47° × 0.47° 96 408 × 96 20 Hz 21 Up to +60 °C 120° 0.47° × 0.47° 96 285 × 96 20 Hz
  • Configurations 20 and 21 reduce the horizontal field of view so that the device can operate at higher ambient temperatures (up to +55 °C and +60 °C).
  • Ambient image: a passive, narrow-band image around 905 nm from the LiDAR receiver, not a camera image. Brightness can differ from what you see; for example, LED-lit areas may look dark. The table shows the image size that matches the point cloud. The maximum image size is 592 × 192 px (configurations 1 to 3), 773 × 192 (4), 1184 × 192 (10 and 11), 2369 × 192 (12), 408 × 192 (20), and 285 × 192 (21).
  • Interlaced configurations (10 to 12): 10 and 11 combine 2 scans (about 100 ms at 20 Hz), 12 combines 4 (about 200 ms). This is the acquisition span, not the output latency. Because the points of one frame are captured at different times, moving objects can appear offset; for moving scenes, validate the result or use a non-interlaced configuration. The mean filter has no effect, and the particle filter should be checked because it compares measurements at different angles.
  • Small objects must be hit repeatedly for reliable measurement. Objects below the minimum object size may need a stationary sensor and target.

Date and system time tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

Date and system time

The time base can be set using various methods:

  • Explicitly setting the time with date, time
  • Transferring the time from the computer used
  • Via an external NTP server (Network Time Protocol) that is accessible in the network.
  • Via an external PTP (Precision Time Protocol) master that is accessible in the network.

NTP uses UDP port 123 and PTP uses UDP ports 319/320. Both are inactive by default. Use PTP when point clouds must be fused with other sensors, because it gives the tightest synchronisation. For background and setup, see Time synchronization.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
Clean up the scan before it leaves the sensor by suppressing extra echoes, artefacts and airborne particles.

Example filter settings in the multiScan270 web interface. Select parameters according to the requirements of each application.

Filters can be combined freely. Active filters run one after another, each on the result of the previous one, in this order: echo filter, particle filter, interval filter, blooming filter, angle-range filter. Keep in mind:

  • Filters apply to both measurement data output and field evaluation. Filtered values cannot be converted back into the original measurements.
  • Each active filter adds processing time and therefore output latency. The particle filter adds a delay of one scan.
  • Field evaluation always uses a single echo. If the echo filter is set to All echoes, field evaluation uses the first echo.
  • In interlaced scan configurations (10 to 12), the precision mode has no effect, and the particle filter compares measurements from different angular positions. Check that it still works as intended in your application.

The signal path through the filters:

flowchart LR
    echo([Echo]) --> core[Measurement core]
    core --> echofilter[Echo filter]
    echofilter --> particle[Particle filter]
    particle --> interval[Interval filter]
    interval --> blooming[Blooming filter]
    blooming --> angle[Angle-range filter]
    angle --> output[Measurement data output]
    angle --> fieldeval[Field evaluation]

Filter processing order for measurement data output and field evaluation.

The precision mode is the multiScan200 version of the mean filter.

For detailed behavior and examples, see Filter details.

docs.title: Inertial Measuring Unit (IMU)
docs.text:
Use the IMU view to inspect the sensor's current orientation and acceleration.

Live capture from a multiScan270's web interface.

Inertial measuring unit (IMU) tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

The IMU view displays the yaw, pitch, and roll angles in degrees, together with the measured acceleration on the X, Y, and Z axes in meters per second squared.

The IMU samples at 100 Hz. It sits at X = −17 mm and Y = +23.5 mm relative to the optical origin, so apply this offset when you fuse IMU data with the point cloud. IMU data is streamed separately in Compact format on TCP port 2117, or as the imu topic over Native ROS 2.

Orientation follows DIN ISO 8855 with a right-handed coordinate system. X is the main viewing direction, and Z points to the top of the device. Measurement data is always output in the device coordinate system. Mounting settings describe the sensor pose in the world coordinate system; without them, both systems are identical.

docs.title: Contamination Indication
docs.text:
Monitor the optics cover for dirt and get a warning before measurement quality drops.

Contamination indication tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

A contamination warning makes LED2/LED4 flash yellow while LED1/LED3 stay green. A contamination error makes LED1/LED3 flash red and LED2/LED4 flash yellow. The contamination state is also available as secondary data, so a host can react before measurement quality drops.

If the measurement data shows anomalies, clean the optics cover first:

  1. If possible, disconnect the power supply.
  2. Clean the optics cover with a clean, damp, lint-free cloth and a mild, antistatic plastic cleaner. Do not use pointed objects.
  3. Remove dust from the housing with a soft brush.

If the optics cover is scratched or damaged, take the device out of operation and have it repaired by SICK.

docs.title: Connection Options
docs.text:
Give the sensor its permanent Ethernet identity so it fits your network.

Ethernet tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

The factory default IP address is 192.168.0.1. The Ethernet link runs at 1 Gbit/s. Keep this in mind for high-resolution scan configurations.

  • After changing the static IP address, restart the device so that Native ROS 2 topics are published correctly.
  • The addressing mode, IP address, subnet mask, default gateway and device name are also cloned to the system plug when you save permanently. A replacement device on the same system plug starts with the same network identity.

docs.title: Inputs and Outputs
docs.text:
Configure the multifunction I/O ports and map field-evaluation results and device states to physical outputs.

Live capture from a multiScan270's web interface.

System plug tile on the port configuration page, captured live from a multiScan270.

The device has up to eight multifunction ports, depending on the mounted system plug. Each port can be configured as an input, with a debounce time, or as an output in push-pull, NPN, or PNP mode. For the electrical values, see the product page on sick.com.

docs.title: Data Output
docs.text:
Decide what measurement data leaves the sensor and how it is streamed to your system.

Measurement data output tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

Data reduction tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

Angular range filter tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

For detailed filter behavior, see Filter details.

Scan data structure: at each horizontal angle step (slot M−1, M, M+1, …), the sensor measures one vertical column with layers 1 to N. The scan configuration sets the number of layers and the angle between slots.

The device streams measurement data in these ways:

Measurement and IMU data outputs, transports, and payloads on the multiScan270.

Output Transport Content Compact TCP 2115 (outgoing) Distance and RSSI, optional ambient light (telegram type 6) Compact TCP 2116 (outgoing) Ambient light only (telegram type 3) Compact IMU TCP 2117 (outgoing) IMU data at 100 Hz (telegram type 7) Native ROS 2 DDS over UDP 7400–65399 PointCloud2, LaserScan, ambient_light and imu topics

All outputs are disabled by default. Compact uses TCP to avoid data loss. Measurement data output responds within 100 ms or less, plus network delay from cables and switches. For each echo, the device also outputs a relative signal strength indicator (RSSI). Its representation depends on the output format: Compact carries an unsigned 16-bit value, while Native ROS 2 PointCloud2 intensity is normalized to 0.0–1.0 and identifies reflectors through the properties bit mask. Native ROS 2 LaserScan and MultiEchoLaserScan intensity uses 0.0–1.0 for natural targets and 1.05 for detected reflectors. Do not use intensity alone to determine whether a measurement is valid. See RSSI values and Native ROS 2 topics for the format-specific details.

For Native ROS 2, use CycloneDDS as the ROS middleware and subscribe only to the topics you need, because subscribed topics are published even when they contain no points. Parameterisation still runs over REST or CoLa. See Compact format and Native ROS 2.

docs.title: Field Evaluation
docs.text:
Configure monitored volumes and let the sensor evaluate incoming 3D scan points on the device.

Live capture from a multiScan270's web interface.

Field evaluation tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

Define a field's polygonal contour and its lower and upper Z limits to form a monitored volume in the sensor coordinate system. The sensor evaluates points inside that volume using the configured detection criteria. Evaluation groups organize the fields and control their activation; results can be combined with logic and mapped to outputs.

  • Up to 48 fields can be configured, and up to 20 can be active at the same time.
  • A group is activated by digital inputs, by telegram, or is always active. Each field in a group has its own evaluation settings.
  • The result can be linked to a switching output and combined with other signals using logic such as AND, OR and XOR.
  • Typical uses are collision protection, object protection and access monitoring.

Evaluation runs after every scan cycle, and the field status is output within 175 ms or less. The latency also depends on where and when an object enters the field relative to the laser position, and on the number of active fields, the digital outputs, the filters and measurement data streaming.

Only points that fall inside an active field add system load, but many active fields can still cause performance problems. If you need more fields at once, reduce the load by disabling the GUI live view, unused data outputs or filters. Test with your actual application.

For programmatic access, see Field evaluation and distance API.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Operating information tile, captured live from a multiScan270.

The device logs events continuously. Logging cannot be switched off; when the log memory is full, the oldest entries are overwritten. Download the diagnostic file from Diagnostics and attach it to any support request, together with the type code and serial number from the type label.

Common device and web-interface symptoms and recommended diagnostic actions.

Symptom Action Both LEDs flash red Device error. Read the error code in the web interface and fix the cause. All LEDs flash red The device may not detect the system plug. Check that it is mounted, clean and dry. All LEDs stay red at start-up Check the power supply; it may not deliver enough current or voltage for motor start. All LEDs are off Check the power supply, and check whether the LEDs were switched off in the interface. The loading screen stays on Reconnect. If that does not help, restart the device. The web interface does not open Check the IP addresses of the device and network adapter, for example with device search. Measurement data shows anomalies Clean the optics cover.

docs.title: Detection History
docs.text: Live capture from a multiScan270's web interface.

docs.title: Release Notes
docs.text: This page documents the multiScan200 firmware release history. Use it to assess update impact and decide whether a release is relevant to your installed firmware and application.

docs.title: Firmware V1.1.0
docs.text:
Compatible with: multiScan270; Release type: Initial release

Initial firmware release for the multiScan200.

docs.title: On-Device Applications
docs.text:
Use sensor-side processing to obtain application results without processing every scan point on a host. Check each page for supported devices and limits.

  • Field Evaluation: configure evaluation fields and read their results.
  • Object Evaluation: use multiScan100 object properties to make decisions based on object criteria.
  • Perpendicular Distance Measurement: measure distance relative to a reference plane.
  • Contamination Indication: monitor dirt on the optics cover.
  • 3D Scan Recording: record a 3D point cloud with a rotating 2D sensor.

docs.title: 3D Scan Recording
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 picoScan100

3D scan recording turns a rotating 2D LiDAR into a 3D scanner without host-side geometry code. While the sensor rotates on an axis, it combines consecutive 2D scans with the rotation angle and stores one point cloud as a .pcd file on the device. The angle comes from the built-in IMU or from an encoder on the axis. Open the result in CloudCompare.

The device keeps only the most recent point cloud, and there is no continuous 3D output. For continuous 3D data or custom transforms, process the scans on the host as described in 3D With 2D LiDARs.

Live capture of the 3D scan recording interface on a picoScan100.

docs.title: Record in SOPASair
docs.text:
1. Mount the sensor so its scan plane sweeps the area of interest as it rotates.
  2. Open Application → 3D scan recording, select the rotation source (IMU or encoder), and enter the sensor offset from the rotation axis.
  3. Start the recording, rotate the sensor through the sweep, and stop the recording.
  4. Download the point cloud when saving is complete.

docs.title: Record over the REST API
docs.text:
Writing parameters and calling methods requires challenge-response authentication.

Record over the REST API: parameter and values.

Parameter Values ScanMergerEnabled true / false ScanMergerSource 0 IMU, 1 ENCODER ScanMergeTrigger 0 METHOD; on the LRS4000 also 1 DIGITAL_INPUT RotationOffset {x, y, z} in mm: sensor offset from the rotation axis
  1. Write the parameters and persist them with POST /api/WriteEeprom.
  2. picoScan150 only: POST /api/ResetScanMergeView to clear the previous recording.
  3. POST /api/StartScanMerge and move the axis through the sweep. With ScanMergeTrigger = 1, a digital input starts and stops the recording instead.
  4. POST /api/StopScanMerge.
  5. picoScan150 only: poll GET /api/MergeSaving until it changes from true back to false.
  6. Download the point cloud. On the picoScan150, use port 80 outside /api/: curl http://192.168.0.1/cloud.pcd -o cloud.pcd. On the LRS4000, download it in SOPASair under Application → 3D scan recording.

The endpoints are listed in the LRS4000 and picoScan100 REST API references. For a complete example, see the House 3D Capture project.

docs.title: Contamination Indication
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

Contamination indication monitors the sensor's optics cover for dirt that could reduce measurement quality. It evaluates contamination per sector of the optics cover, so maintenance can target the affected area before the optics become too dirty. The number of sectors depends on the device. The SOPASair sector display shows where contamination is accumulating, with overall states such as Clean, Minor, Heavy, and Blocked.

Contamination indication tile in SOPASair, captured live from a multiScan270: overall status, sector display, and configuration.

Configure the sensitivity, response time, warning threshold, and active sectors for the installation. The device can expose the result through its GUI and REST API; depending on configuration, it can also be monitored through CoLa or mapped to digital outputs. The warning and error behavior, and whether blocked sectors count as errors, are configurable. Use the indication as a maintenance signal and inspect and clean the optics according to the product documentation.

All contamination settings and results are available through the REST API. The endpoints are listed under Contamination Indication in the LRS4000 REST API, multiScan100 REST API, multiScan200 REST API, and picoScan100 REST API references.

Writes require the Authorized Client user level and challenge-response authentication. Persist configuration changes with WriteEeprom; otherwise, they may be lost after a power cycle.

picoScan100 CoLa clients can read configuration and sector data and subscribe to event-driven contamination updates. See the picoScan100 CoLa Telegram Listing. For the interface walkthrough, see Contamination Indication in SOPASair.

picoScan100 example: Compare optics-cover contamination states with the sector indications described above.

docs.title: Field Evaluation
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

The sensor evaluates detection zones on the device. Field evaluation checks whether scan points enter a configured polygon and reports whether the field is free or infringed. The result can drive a digital output and can be read through REST, CoLa, or WebSocket events. In SOPASair, field evaluation is the Object Detection application; both names mean the same function.

Field Evaluation: term and meaning.

Term Meaning Evaluation One field (polygon) with its detection parameters, stored in an evaluation slot Evaluation slot Numbered storage place for one evaluation, for example Eval001 Group One or more evaluations that are activated together Activation type When a group is evaluated: always, by digital inputs, or by telegram Result Per evaluation: free or infringed; per group: active, inactive, or not configured

picoScan100: How to draw fields and detect objects?

docs.title: Configure in the Web GUI
docs.text:
Open the Object Detection application in SOPASair to create and edit polygon points directly. This is the quickest method for commissioning and manual adjustments. The field editor also supports teach-in.

Field evaluation teach-in tile in SOPASair.

For bulk coordinate changes, open the Field settings dialog and select JSON in its footer toolbar. The editor switches from the coordinate table to a JSON text field. Paste the prepared polygon to replace all points at once:

{
  "points": [
    { "x": -5, "y": 531 },
    { "x": 837, "y": 565 },
    { "x": 907, "y": -637 },
    { "x": 12, "y": -590 }
  ]
}

docs.title: Copy to Other Devices
docs.text: Use the top-right SOPASair menu to download the complete configuration from a commissioned sensor. It includes field geometries and can be imported into another compatible device, making it suitable for repeatable commissioning and replacement devices. Keep a versioned, validated backup for each deployed configuration.

docs.title: Teach In
docs.text:
Teach-in captures the current environment and uses the measured contour as a field for object detection. Use it during commissioning when the surrounding geometry should define the detection field instead of drawing a polygon manually.

Open the Object Detection application in SOPASair and select Teach-in in the field configuration. Set the distances in front of and behind the object, choose the minimum teach-in time, and click Start. Stop the teach-in when the environment has been captured, then save the field evaluation configuration.

Teach-in configuration in SOPASair.

The configured distances take effect during the next teach-in. Keep the intended environment stable while the contour is captured.

Teach-in uses the same evaluation group and output mechanism as a manually configured field. After the contour has been captured, monitor the evaluation result through the configured output, REST, CoLa, or WebSocket events.

docs.title: Minimum Object Size
docs.text:
The farther an object is, the wider apart the beams are, so small objects can fall between them. Select a device family, scan configuration, target, and object size to estimate up to which range the object is still detected. Device presets fill in the model-specific values from the operating instructions. Select Custom Values to adjust angular resolution, beam divergence, minimum spot size, and scanning range.

Input

Device ?

Select the device family, or Custom Values to enter your own geometry and scanning range.

Scan configuration ?

Select the model and scan mode. Presets fill in the operating-instruction values. Interlaced modes combine several frames and require a stationary scene.

Target ?

Target reflectance limits the scanning range: 10% is dark, 90% is bright. Reflector ranges assume a suitable reflector. Preset conditions must match your application.

Angular resolution, horizontal [°] ?

Horizontal angle between measurement directions. A smaller step generally allows smaller objects at the same distance. Editable in Custom Values.

Angular resolution, vertical [°] ?

Angle between scan layers used for the height calculation. Real layer gaps can vary; the multiScan165 preset uses 2.5°, while outer gaps can reach 5°.

Beam divergence, horizontal [mrad] ?

Horizontal beam spread in milliradians, used to display spot width. A preset may include the scan-mode contribution. Blank means no verified value for this mode.

Beam divergence, vertical [mrad] ?

Vertical beam spread in milliradians, used to display spot height. For LRS4000, the vertical spot also determines the height check.

Minimum spot size [mm] ?

Initial beam diameter used by the custom model for both axes. It sets the minimum object-size floor and the starting spot size.

Scanning range [m] ?

Maximum usable range for your target and operating conditions. This caps the geometric result in Custom Values.

Object width [mm] ?

Width presented to the sensor across the scan direction. Use the smallest relevant width, accounting for the object's orientation.

Object height [mm] ?

Height presented to the sensor. The height check uses layer spacing, or the vertical spot for LRS4000. Enter 0 to disable this check. picoScan presets are width-only.

Required beam spacings across the object ?

One spacing uses the operating-instruction minimum-size model. Larger values add a planning margin and reduce range; they are not a guaranteed number of detected returns.

12345

Result

Maximum range ?

Smallest of the width limit, enabled height limit and target scanning range. This is a geometric planning estimate, not a detection guarantee.

– Range limit from the width ?

Geometric range supported by the entered width, before applying the height check or target scanning-range cap.

– Range limit from the height ?

Geometric range supported by the entered height, before applying the width check or target scanning-range cap. Height 0 disables this check.

– Scanning range for the target ?

Preset range cap for the selected target. picoScan diffuse-target values are typical at 10 klx; multiScan100 values use 10 klx. Footnote 1 marks a working-range fallback, not a specified target range.

– Minimum object width at maximum range ?

Minimum width from the selected model at the calculated maximum range. If no positive range exists, it is shown at the scanning-range cap instead.

– Minimum object height at maximum range ?

Minimum height at the calculated range, using layer gaps or the LRS4000 vertical spot. Shown only when the height check is enabled. The multiScan model follows the published size table.

– Spot width at maximum range ?

Horizontal beam footprint at the calculated range: initial spot plus divergence times distance. This is separate from the minimum object width. Blank means the preset has no verified divergence for this mode.

– Spot height at maximum range ?

Vertical beam footprint at the calculated range: initial spot plus vertical divergence times distance. A 2D scanner still has a vertical beam footprint.

–

1) Not specified for this target; the working range is shown.

Minimum object size over the range. The maximum range is where the curve reaches the object size, capped by the scanning range for the selected target.

These results are estimates only. Testing the individual object in its actual position and operating conditions is necessary; the calculator does not guarantee detection. The LRS4000, multiScan100, and picoScan100 presets use the corresponding model-specific operating-instruction data and formulas.

docs.title: Activate and Monitor a Group
docs.text:
Activate and Monitor a Group: REST resource and purpose.

REST resource Purpose ActivateEvaluationGroup Activates or deactivates a TELEGRAM-controlled group FieldEvaluationGroupState Group state: not configured, active, or inactive FieldEvaluationResult Current result: FREE, INFRINGED, or a transitional state; also available as a WebSocket event

A typical application creates the groups once, persists the configuration, and at runtime reads the group state and result, updates contours when necessary, and switches telegram-controlled groups.

For full payloads, see the LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, and picoScan100 REST API references and the CoLa telegram listings for LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, and picoScan100.

Activation types (Activation.Type of a group). ActivateEvaluationGroup only switches TELEGRAM groups:

Activate and Monitor a Group: value, type, and behavior.

Value Type Behavior 0 Deactivated The group is never evaluated. 1 Always The group is active as soon as it is stored. ActivateEvaluationGroup returns false for it and cannot switch it off. 2 Inputs Digital inputs activate the group. 3 Telegram The group starts in the state set by InitialActivationStateTelegram and is switched with ActivateEvaluationGroup.

FieldEvaluationGroupState returns one value per group: 0 not configured, 1 active, 2 inactive. FieldEvaluationResult returns one state per evaluation: 0 not configured, 1 inactive, 2 free, 3 detecting infringed, 4 infringed, 5 detecting free.

docs.title: Configure over the API
docs.text:
On all devices, create the evaluations in SOPASair or restore them from a configuration file; REST and CoLa can then change them. On the picoScan100, REST and CoLa can also build complete evaluations from scratch. The following workflow applies to picoScan150 with firmware V2.3.3. Some of these variables, such as Eval001–Eval048 and EvaluationGroupMapping, are not listed in the published OpenAPI file, but can be read and written as REST variables (GET / POST /api/<Variable>).

Configure over the API: variable or method, purpose, and devices.

Variable or method Purpose Devices Eval001–Eval048 Detection parameters of one evaluation slot: mode, minimum object size, timing, and the referenced volume (VolumeList) picoScan100 SetFieldEvaluationContour / GetFieldEvaluationContour Writes or reads the polygon of an evaluation LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan100 SetFieldEvaluationConfiguration / GetFieldEvaluationConfiguration Writes or reads evaluation parameters multiScan200 EvaluationGroupMapping Groups evaluations and sets the activation type of each group picoScan100 EvaluationGroupType Selects field evaluation or perpendicular-distance mode LRS4000, picoScan100 PortConfiguration Assigns an evaluation result to a digital output LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan100 WriteEeprom (REST) / mEEwriteall (CoLa) Stores the configuration permanently LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan100

To create an evaluation on the picoScan100, log in as Authorized client or Service and write the variables in this order:

  1. Write EvalNNN with the detection mode, the minimum object size, and VolumeList = [NNN].
  2. Write the polygon with SetFieldEvaluationContour. It returns error 1 (invalid evaluation) if VolumeList of the slot is empty, so write the slot first.
  3. Write EvaluationGroupMapping. The whole array is replaced on every write: read the current mapping first and include every group you want to keep.
  4. Optional: write PortConfiguration to switch a digital output when the evaluation is infringed. Outputs refer to evaluations (sources EG01–EG48), not to groups, and the whole port array must be written.
  5. Call WriteEeprom. The device re-initializes; wait about 1 s before reading the state.
  6. For a TELEGRAM group, switch it on with ActivateEvaluationGroup.

To delete an evaluation, remove its group from EvaluationGroupMapping, clear VolumeList and the name of the slot, and call WriteEeprom. The group state returns to not configured.

The coordinates are in millimeters in the sensor coordinate system: x points forward (depth) and y to the side.

Detection modes (EvaluationParamsCommon.Mode of the evaluation slot):

Configure over the API: value, mode, and the field is infringed when.

Value Mode The field is infringed when 0 Blanking An object at least as large as the minimum object size is inside the field. This is the most common mode. 1 Reflector only A highly reflective object such as a retroreflector is inside the field. 2 Contour The scan deviates from the taught-in contour by more than the tolerance. Requires a valid teach-in.

docs.title: Change a Polygon
docs.text:
The REST API exposes SetFieldEvaluationContour to update a polygon. The evaluation must already exist. Use GetFieldEvaluationContour to confirm the stored geometry and persist the change with WriteEeprom. See the REST client example.

CoLa provides the same SetFieldEvaluationContour function through its telegram interface. Use it when the integration already uses CoLa, such as a PLC or legacy client; see CoLa.

The sick_perception_sdk uses the REST interface and provides an application-level option for changing contours. See the object-detection example.

docs.title: Teach in over the API
docs.text:
A teach-in evaluation is an evaluation slot with mode 2 (contour). The polygon written with SetFieldEvaluationContour is not the detection field: it is the region of interest in which teach-in learns the reference contour. GetFieldEvaluationContour therefore returns this region, not the learned contour.

Teach-in is global; it is not bound to an evaluation slot. Set the parameters, then start and stop the teach-in:

Teach in over the API: variable or method and purpose.

Variable or method Purpose TeachInToleranceFront / TeachInToleranceBack Tolerance in front of and behind the taught contour, in mm (default 250) TeachInMinimumTimeMs Minimum teach-in time, 100 to 60000 ms (default 250) TeachInActivationInput Digital input that starts the teach-in; 0 = software only StartTeachIn / StopTeachIn Starts and stops the teach-in TeachInActive 1 while the teach-in runs TeachInContourValid 1 after a teach-in produced a valid contour

Keep the scene stable for at least the minimum teach-in time, stop the teach-in, check TeachInContourValid, and call WriteEeprom. To change the field later, repeat the teach-in, for example with a larger tolerance; the region of interest stays the same.

docs.title: Distance-Dependent
docs.text:
The Distance-dependent parameter determines whether two detected objects are evaluated separately or merged into one object based on their axial separation. It works with the configured Blanking width to avoid triggering a field evaluation when separate small objects would otherwise appear as one large object.

picoScan100: 2D Object Detection Parameter Distance-dependent.

The video uses two objects: a foreground object approximately 60 mm wide, a background object approximately 250 mm wide, and about 450 mm of axial separation. The standard blanking width is 300 mm.

Example: configuration, result, and explanation.

Configuration Result Explanation Distance-dependent off Field infringed Both objects merge into one contiguous object wider than 300 mm. Distance-dependent on; threshold 300 mm Field not infringed The objects are at least 300 mm apart and are evaluated separately; neither is wider than 300 mm. Distance-dependent on; threshold 500 mm Field infringed The objects are less than 500 mm apart, so they merge and exceed the blanking width.

Set the separation threshold to the distance at which nearby objects should be merged for your application.

docs.title: Ground Filter (multiScan100)
docs.text:
The ground filter uses upper and lower ground thresholds to reduce false field-evaluation triggers caused by the ground. When configured correctly, it retains small objects such as forklift tines and can be used indoors and outdoors. The filter also affects perpendicular-distance evaluations. See Ground Filter for availability and API settings.

multiScan1xx: Ground-filter behavior in a field application.

docs.title: Object Evaluation
docs.text:
Compatible with: multiScan100

Object Evaluation combines 3D object tracking with configurable criteria. The tracker estimates each object's track ID, horizontal and vertical size, speed, direction of movement, and age. An evaluation checks those properties within a configured region and reports whether its criteria are met. This lets an application respond to relevant movement without processing every scan point on a host.

Your browser does not support embedded video. Download the Object Evaluation overview video.

multiScan100 Object Evaluation overview: tracked objects are evaluated against configured regions and criteria.

The multiScan100 3D view displays tracked-object IDs, dimensions, speed, direction of movement, and age alongside the configured evaluation regions.

Object Evaluation is available from multiScan100 firmware 2.5.0 and requires the 3D Object Detection Advanced package. Check the device variant, firmware, and installed license before commissioning. See the firmware 2.5.0 release notes and multiScan100 license list.

Object Evaluation filters tracked objects by measurable properties; it does not return semantic object-class labels. Validate any application decision against the real objects and operating conditions.

docs.title: How an Evaluation Works
docs.text:
Object tracking estimates object properties over successive scans. An evaluation then applies its spatial region and criteria to those tracks. The result is a state for each configured evaluation, not a class label for each object.

Object Evaluation criteria: region and track properties used to determine whether an evaluation is infringed.

Criterion How it affects the evaluation Region of interest A polygon in the scan plane, with lower and upper Z limits, defines where objects are evaluated. Object size Minimum horizontal and vertical sizes can be set. An optional maximum-size filter rejects objects that exceed the configured maximum dimensions. Motion state ALL accepts moving and stationary tracks; MOVING or STATIONARY restricts the evaluation to that motion state. Speed An optional minimum and maximum speed range filters tracks. Direction An optional direction filter uses a configured direction and uncertainty range. Object age A minimum age can exclude tracks until they have been observed long enough. Hidden time A maximum hidden time controls how long a temporarily unobserved track can remain part of the evaluation.

Use SOPASair for the displayed units and the multiScan100 REST API reference for numeric constraints and enum values. The REST configuration uses EvaluationId to associate a contour and criteria with an evaluation.

docs.title: Configure and Validate
docs.text:
1. Confirm that the sensor has firmware 2.5.0 or later and the 3D Object Detection Advanced package.
  2. In Configuration > Basic settings, turn off interlaced mode. Object evaluation is unavailable in interlaced mode; the sensor reports error 211.
  3. Open the Object Evaluation application in SOPASair. Define the region of interest and choose the motion, size, speed, direction, and age criteria that match the application.
  4. Activate the configured evaluation group. A group can be activated or deactivated through the REST API as well as the device interface.
  5. Test representative objects and movements in the intended region. Confirm that qualifying tracks produce the expected result and that excluded tracks do not.
  6. Monitor the application, group, configuration, and evaluation states described below.

docs.title: Read and Interpret Results
docs.text:
Use these read-only REST endpoints to check whether the application is available, the group is active, and the evaluation result matches the scene.

Object Evaluation status endpoints: REST path and returned status.

REST endpoint Meaning GET /api/ObjectEvaluationApplicationState Application state: 0 DEACTIVATED, 1 ACTIVE, 2 CONFIGURING, or 3 ERROR. GET /api/ObjectEvaluationGroupState Activation state for configured groups: 0 NOT_CONFIGURED, 1 ACTIVE, or 2 INACTIVE. GET /api/ObjectEvaluationResult Results for configured evaluations. EvaluationResultList contains one state per evaluation. GET /api/ObjectEvaluationConfigState Reports whether active beam and evaluation limits are 0 OK, 1 WARNING, or 2 EXCEEDED.

Each state in EvaluationResultList has a distinct meaning:

Evaluation result states: numeric value and interpretation.

Value State Meaning 0 NOT_CONFIGURED No evaluation is configured for this entry. 1 INACTIVE The evaluation is configured but not active. 2 FREE No qualifying object infringes the evaluation. 3 DETECTING_INFRINGED The sensor is confirming an infringement. 4 INFRINGED A qualifying object infringes the evaluation. 5 DETECTING_FREE The sensor is confirming that the infringement has cleared.

Treat DETECTING_INFRINGED and DETECTING_FREE as transitional states, not stable results. The application state, group state, configuration state, and per-evaluation result are separate. Check the relevant status endpoints when diagnosing an unexpected output.

docs.title: Configure Through REST
docs.text:
The REST API provides operations to get and set each evaluation's contour and criteria, and to activate or deactivate a group. The get/set contour and configuration operations require at least the Authorized Client user level. Review the request schemas and error codes in the multiScan100 REST API reference before writing configuration.

Object Evaluation configuration operations: REST method and purpose.

REST operation Purpose POST /api/GetObjectEvaluationContour Read an evaluation's polygon and lower/upper Z limits. POST /api/SetObjectEvaluationContour Set an evaluation's polygon and lower/upper Z limits. POST /api/GetObjectEvaluationConfiguration Read an evaluation's name and criteria. POST /api/SetObjectEvaluationConfiguration Set an evaluation's name and criteria. POST /api/ActivateObjectEvaluationGroup Activate or deactivate an evaluation group.

The Get... operations above use HTTP POST with an evaluation ID in the request body. Do not confuse them with the read-only GET status endpoints. After changing settings, read them back and verify the live result in SOPASair.

docs.title: Configure Through CoLa
docs.text:
The same status variables and operations are available as CoLa telegrams, for example for a PLC. See the Object Evaluation telegrams in the multiScan100 CoLa telegram listing for the structures and copyable CoLa A and CoLa B examples.

ActivateObjectEvaluationGroup switches only groups with the activation type Telegram. For a group with the activation type Always, the device confirms the request, but the group stays active. Read ObjectEvaluationGroupState to confirm the change. Changes made through CoLa or REST are lost on restart unless you save them permanently.

docs.title: Perpendicular Distance Measurement
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 picoScan100

Perpendicular distance evaluation measures object distances relative to a reference line in the scan plane. Define a field and reference line in the application; the sensor evaluates the points in that field and reports the minimum and maximum perpendicular distances and the positions of the corresponding measuring points.

multiScan1xx: Perpendicular distance application demonstration.

docs.title: Configure a Measurement
docs.text:
1. Open Application > Perpendicular distance measurement in SOPASair and add an evaluation group.
  2. Draw the zone in which objects should be measured.
  3. Set Max. blanking size and Detection time under Object detection to balance measurement stability and response time for the target.
  4. Save the configuration to the device.
  5. Check the live minimum and maximum distances and their measuring-point coordinates in the result list.

The evaluation runs on the sensor, so the host receives measurement results without having to detect objects from the raw scan itself. See the SOPASair configuration walkthrough for the interface details.

picoScan100 example: Output a field's perpendicular distance after configuring the measurement field; use the interfaces below to read the results in your application.

docs.title: Read Results
docs.text:
The REST endpoint GET /api/perpendicularDistanceResult returns a timestamp and an evaluations array. Each result contains an evaluation ID, minimum and maximum distance, and the 3D position of each corresponding measuring point. The evaluations array is empty when no object is measured. The result is read-only; see the picoScan100 REST API reference.

CoLa clients can poll sRN perpendicularDistanceResult for the current measurement or subscribe with sEN perpendicularDistanceResult for event updates. The telegram reports the shortest and furthest measuring point in the range relative to the reference plane. See the picoScan100 CoLa Telegram Listing.

docs.title: Configure over the API (picoScan100)
docs.text:
REST and CoLa expose every variable needed to create, change, and delete a perpendicular distance evaluation without SOPASair. The following workflow applies to picoScan150 with firmware V2.3.3. Some of these variables are not listed in the published OpenAPI file, but can be read and written as REST variables (GET / POST /api/<Variable>).

A perpendicular distance evaluation has two parts, as in SOPASair:

Configure over the API (picoScan100): part, variables, and content.

Part Variables Content Object detection EvalNNN, VolumeNNN Detection parameters (blanking mode, minimum object size, detection time) and the field in which objects are measured Reference line perpDistNNN Normal vector of the line in the scan plane and its signed distance from the sensor, in mm

To create an evaluation, log in as Authorized client or Service and write the variables in this order, using the same slot number NNN throughout:

  1. Set the slot to perpendicular distance: write EvaluationGroupType with all 48 values and 1 at the slot position (0 = field evaluation).
  2. Write EvalNNN with VolumeList = [NNN].
  3. Write the field polygon directly to VolumeNNN. Do not use SetFieldEvaluationContour here: it returns success for perpendicular distance slots but is not reliable for them.
  4. Write the reference line to perpDistNNN. The normal vector sets the orientation, for example (1, 0, 0) for a line across the forward direction, and the distance sets its position. Because the picoScan100 is a 2D sensor, the z component is always 0. The no-data mode sets the output when no object is measured: 0 zero, 1 hold the last value, or 2 a user-defined substitution distance.
  5. Add the group to EvaluationGroupMapping with EvalIds = [NNN]. The whole array is replaced on every write, so include every group you want to keep.
  6. Call WriteEeprom and wait about 1 s before reading the result.

Keep in mind:

  • Perpendicular distance groups need their own slots; they cannot share a slot with a field evaluation group.
  • If the field is missing (empty VolumeList or empty VolumeNNN) or the group references no evaluation, the device reports a recoverable error (DeviceStatus = 7 instead of 3) and the result stays empty.
  • Perpendicular distance results are not assigned to digital outputs; read them from perpendicularDistanceResult.
  • Group activation (ALWAYS, INPUTS, TELEGRAM) and ActivateEvaluationGroup work as for field evaluation.

To delete the evaluation, remove the group from EvaluationGroupMapping, clear EvalNNN, VolumeNNN, and perpDistNNN, set the slot in EvaluationGroupType back to 0, and call WriteEeprom.

For output and evaluation-group concepts shared with field evaluation, see Field Evaluation.

docs.title: picoScan100
docs.text:
The picoScan100 is a compact 2D LiDAR sensor with one scan plane and a 276° scan range. It comes in two variants: the picoScan120 and the picoScan150. For a sensor and cable combination to get started, see the Starter Kit.

Specifications and data sheet on sick.com

picoScan150: one 276° scan plane. Blue represents infrared; beam geometry, wall hits, and speed are schematic.

Search for picoScan100 on sick.com and open the Downloads tab of your device variant's product page for firmware, EPLAN and CAD data, and available NVIDIA Isaac Sim models and Milestone XProtect plug-ins. Select the files for your device variant; see Licenses for feature availability and Release Notes for firmware changes.

  • CoLa A/B
  • Digital inputs
  • Ethernet
  • HTTPS
  • NTP
  • PTP

Inputs, onboard processing, and outputs of the picoScan100. Each column is an independent list.

Use the Product ID (PID) to find the exact product variant on sick.com: enter the part number (P/N) and optional serial number (S/N), for example 1134610/25250710. A complete pid.sick.com URL is also accepted.

Product ID pid.sick.com/ Open product

docs.title: API | CoLa Telegrams
docs.text:
This reference lists the CoLa telegrams supported by the picoScan100. Use the command details to build or troubleshoot PLC and other low-level integrations without guessing the telegram structure.

Examples are grouped by protocol, with each telegram representation in a separate code block and its own copy button.

Categories follow the picoScan150 REST API reference where corresponding CoLa telegrams are available. Select a telegram to expand its structure and examples. A direct link to a telegram opens it automatically. The categories organize the reference; they do not imply that every telegram is supported by every picoScan variant.

docs.title: General
Log In [sMN SetAccessMode]
docs.text:

docs.title: Autostart Measurement [sWN LMPautostartmeas]
docs.text:

docs.title: Set Time Stamp [sMN LSPsetdatetime]
docs.text:
The data format in the telegram is: +2009{SPC}+7{SPC}+22{SPC}+12{SPC}+0{SPC}+0{SPC}+0.The numbers represent year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond.

If plus is used up-front the data it is interpreted as an integer decimal number, without the plus it's the scanner reads the data as hex format.

The answer is always in ASCII format.

Does only work if NTP- respectively PTP-Client is not active.

There is no real time clock inside the device. When the scanner is switched off and after a reboot, the time has to be set again. Therefore, it is recommended to use a NTP or a PTP setting.

Telegram structure: sMN LSPsetdatetime

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary)
Command type Method String 3 sMN 73 4D 4E
Command Set time stamp String 14 LSPsetdatetime 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65
Year Uint_16 2 +1970d … +2099d (07B2h … 0833h) 07 B2 … 08 33
Month Uint_8 1 +1d … +12d(01h … 0Ch) 01 … 0C
Day Uint_8 1 +1d … +31d(01h … 1Fh) 00 … 1F
Hour Uint_8 1 +0d … +23d(00h … 17h) 00 … 17
Minute Uint_8 1 +0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh) 00 … 3B
Second Uint_8 1 +0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh) 00 … 3B
Microsecond Uint_32 4 +0d … +999999d(00000000h … 000F423Fh) 00 00 00 00 … 00 0F 42 3F

docs.title: Send Data Permanently [sEN LMDscandata]
docs.text:
Start/ stop continuous retrievement of measurement data from device. Data will be transmitted as configured as soon as measurement data is generated by the device. Data is transmitted only via LMDscandata when LMDscandata is selected as data output format.

During the boot-up phase of the device, there will be no data telegram or answer from the device.

docs.title: Data Reduction
Set Angle Range Filter [sWN LFPangleRangeFilter]
docs.text:
The angle range filter set up the horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) start- and stop angle in rad.

BeamIncrement = the 'beamIncrement' which is used to subsample the beams within the selected angle range. With a 'beamIncrement' of n only every nth beam from the selected angle range is copied to the output scan, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. If the beamIncrement is zero it is set to one.

docs.text:
Returns the current IMU data (e.g. Acceleration, Orientation, ... ). The data is given in the following coordinate system which is based on the DIN70000 system. The x-axis lies on the 90-degree-beam of the 0-degree-layer. The y-axis is perpendicular to the x-axis and lies in the 0-degree-layer. The y-values are rising in the counterclockwise rotation direction (right-handed system). The z-axis is perpendicular to the x-y-plane and the scanner top points to rising z-values.

docs.title: SOPASair Walkthrough
docs.text: This page describes the picoScan100 web interface and the settings in each view. Use it to commission the sensor before you automate the configuration through the API. To try the interface without a device, open it in the Virtual Sensor Lab.

docs.title: Home
docs.text:
The Home page summarizes the sensor's state: device, connection, measurement, field evaluation, and data-output status, device information with the firmware version, the live scan, and the I/O states. Use it to confirm that the sensor is online and healthy before you change settings.

Live capture of the picoScan100 SOPASair Home page.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Choose the scan configuration and the core measurement behavior. Resolution, frequency, and range trade off against each other.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

The live scan on the left updates as you change the configuration, which is the quickest way to judge a setting.

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text:
Basic Settings controls the scan configuration used by the sensor. The settings are shown on the right; the live scan on the left shows the effect of the selected frequency, angular resolution, and other settings immediately. Use this view to check coverage and measurement behavior while commissioning.

Coordinate System

The device coordinate system uses one point as the origin and reference for all laser beams and distance measurements. With no translation into a world coordinate system, this point is also the world origin.

The horizontal beam angle is theta (θ). A beam at θ = 0° points along the middle of the sensor's main viewing direction, making the scan symmetric around the X axis. The vertical elevation angle is phi (φ) and is measured from the X/Y plane. For a single-plane picoScan, φ = 0° when the sensor is ideally mounted.

Horizontal beam angle theta.

Vertical beam angle phi.

Measurement data is always output in the device coordinate system. Transform it into a world or application frame on the receiving system after accounting for the sensor's mounting position and orientation. See 3D point clouds with 2D LiDARs for an example coordinate transform.

Date and system time

The time base can be set using various methods:

  • Explicitly setting the date and time
  • Transferring the time from the computer used
  • Via an external NTP server (Network Time Protocol) that is accessible in the network. The technology uses UDP on port 123. This setting is recommended to ensure a correct time stamp in the detection history or error entries.
  • Via an external PTP (Precision Time Protocol) master that is accessible in the network. The technology uses UDP on ports 319 and 320. This setting is recommended for precise synchronization requirements (e.g. between several devices).

Dynamic Sensing Profiles

LiDAR applications often need different sensor characteristics at different times. An AMR may need the shortest response time in busy areas, a large scanning range and good angular resolution in a warehouse, and the highest close-range angular resolution while docking. Higher angular resolution requires a lower scanning frequency, so choose the priority for each application.

Dynamic Sensing Profiles allow the scan's core parameters to be changed during operation without restarting the sensor. The Scan Data Configuration function allows fast switching between profiles:

Basic Settings: profile, frequency, angular resolution, and typical use.

Profile Frequency Angular resolution Typical use 1 15 Hz 0.5° Object detection with large scanning ranges 2 15 Hz 0.33° TiM series retrofit 3 20 Hz 0.1° Fine positioning or environment maps 4 20 Hz 0.25° Low-noise measurements; recommended for LiDAR-LOC 5 25 Hz 0.25° LMS100 series retrofit 6 30 Hz 0.1° Fine positioning or environment maps 7 40 Hz 0.25° Fast object detection at a large scanning range 8 50 Hz 0.25° Very fast object detection 9 15 Hz 0.05° Highest angular resolution for static measurements 10 40 Hz 0.125° High angular resolution and high scan rate 11 15 Hz 1° TiM series retrofit

Available profiles depend on the device variant and license; see Licenses.

How to change the device name.

How to change scanning frequency and angular resolution.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
Clean up the scan before it leaves the sensor by suppressing extra echoes, artifacts and airborne particles.

Example filter settings in the picoScan100 web interface. Select parameters according to the requirements of each application.

If present, the filters are applied in the following order:

  1. Fog filter
  2. Echo filter
  3. Particle filter
  4. Moving average filter
  5. Filters for data reduction and the region of interest filter

For detailed behavior and examples, see Filter details.

docs.title: Inertial Measuring Unit (IMU)
docs.text:
Use the IMU view to inspect the sensor's current orientation and acceleration.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

The IMU view displays the yaw, pitch, and roll angles in degrees, together with the measured acceleration on the X, Y, and Z axes in meters per second squared. The orientation indicator provides a visual representation of the current sensor position.

Use these values as a guide when checking the sensor installation or interpreting the scan coordinate system.

docs.title: Contamination Indication
docs.text:
Monitor the optics cover for dirt and get a warning before measurement quality drops.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

The contamination status provides a live reading of Clean, Minor, Heavy, or Blocked. The segment wheel identifies where contamination is accumulating around the optics cover. Configure whether contamination triggers a warning, an error, or both, and adjust the sensitivity and outputs for the environment.

How to receive contamination indication through event-driven CoLa.

docs.title: Connection Options
docs.text:
Give the sensor its permanent Ethernet identity so it fits your network.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

Choose static addressing to enter a fixed IP address, or DHCP to have a server assign the address automatically, according to your application and network requirements. The IP address must be unique on your network. The subnet mask defines which addresses are local, for example 255.255.255.0, and the default gateway provides access to other subnets. The MAC address and calculated speed are read-only values for reference and firewall rules.

  1. Set the addressing mode to Static.
  2. Enter the IP, subnet mask, and gateway for your network.
  3. Press Apply.
  4. Reconnect the browser at the new address.

Pressing Apply drops your current browser connection.

docs.title: Inputs and Outputs
docs.text:
Configure the multifunction I/O ports and map field-evaluation results and device states to physical outputs.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

Set each port as an input or an output and give it a name. Bind an output to a source, such as a field-evaluation result or a device state. Configure the logic (HIGH or LOW active), inversion, restart behavior, and status log. The right panel shows the live status and counters for every port.

I/O is a simple way to connect a PLC when you do not want to parse the data stream.

How to switch digital outputs by API.

docs.title: Data Output
docs.text:
Decide what measurement data leaves the sensor and how it is streamed to your system.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

For data output, select Compact, MSGPACK, LMDscandata, or Native ROS 2 according to your application. For Compact or MSGPACK, configure serialization to include only the RSSI and properties layers your application needs. Reduce bandwidth at the source with an angular-range filter that retains one sector or an interval filter that reduces the number of scans sent per second.

Compact outputs measurement data over UDP and provides separate controls for RSSI and properties serialization.

MSGPACK outputs measurement data over UDP to the configured destination address and port.

LMDscandata provides CoLa ASCII and CoLa Binary TCP ports. Restart the sensor after changing a port.

Native ROS 2 configures the sensor and reference coordinate frames, namespace, and DDS domain ID.

The IMU data output panel enables IMU streaming and configures the destination port and IP address.

The Encoder data output panel enables encoder-data streaming and configures the destination port and IP address.

The Data reduction panel reduces the transmitted data with an interval filter and an angular range filter.

For detailed filter behavior, see Filter details.

For the Compact format, a segment that lies entirely outside the selected range is omitted. A segment that is only partly within the range remains in the output and its outside values are filled with 0.

The Range filter panel limits data by rectangular X/Y coordinates or by minimum and maximum distance.

The scan view shows the selected region of interest and the points detected within it.

docs.title: Field Evaluation
docs.text:
Draw 2D fields in the sensor's scan plane. The sensor detects points inside them without an external computer.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

Each field belongs to an evaluation group that combines field geometry, logic, and output. A field state can drive a physical output (see Inputs and outputs) or appear in the detection list for your software. A group can remain active continuously or be switched by an input, for example to monitor a zone only while a machine is moving. Pan and zoom the scan view to check field coverage across the full aperture angle.

Live capture of creating a detection field on a picoScan100.

  1. On the Field evaluation panel, click Add group to create an evaluation group.
  2. The group opens an evaluation chain: Field → Evaluation → Output.
  3. Click the Field node to define the field geometry: draw a contour, or use Teach-in to capture the current environment as the field.
  4. Set the evaluation logic and wire the result to an output; the field then appears live in the 2D view.
  5. Click the floppy-disk icon in the toolbar to save the configuration permanently (until you do, changes live in RAM and are lost on restart).

The REST API can also create, change, and activate evaluation groups; see Field Evaluation.

  • How to draw fields and detect objects
  • How to use a taught background for field evaluation

How to configure a field for retro-reflectors only.

docs.title: Perpendicular Distance Measurement
docs.text:
Each evaluation group measures the perpendicular distance from the sensor's scan line to the nearest object inside a zone. Like field evaluation, it runs on the sensor, but returns a distance rather than a field-clear/field-infringed state; no raw-scan processing on a host is needed.

Perpendicular distance measurement in SOPASair.

The Max. blanking size setting ignores gaps smaller than the set width, and the Detection time setting sets how long an object must be present (in scans) before it counts.

  1. On the Perpendicular distance measurement panel, click Add group.
  2. Draw the zone the measurement applies to, the same way you draw a field.
  3. Set Max. blanking size and Detection time under Object detection to match your target and required responsiveness.
  4. Read the distance in the Result list for distance measurement, or wire it into your software over the REST API or WebSocket events.
  5. Click the floppy-disk icon to save the configuration permanently (until you do, changes live in RAM and are lost on restart).

The Result list shows the minimum and maximum distance and the coordinates of the measuring points for each evaluation.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
The health dashboard shows device, connection, measurement, and data-output status; the power-on counter, operating hours, temperature, and most recent parameterization; and a filterable event log with message severity, ID, time, and description. You can create and download a diagnostic file for SICK service; creating a new file overwrites the previous one.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

How to read internal device temperature.

docs.title: Cybersecurity
docs.text:
Harden the sensor by managing certificates and switching network services on or off.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

Use this page to create an HTTPS certificate for encrypted access and enable only the required services and protocols, such as CoLa, device search, the web server, HTTPS, or SSH. Each row shows its purpose and physical and logical port to support firewall planning. Disable legacy protocols and developer access in production.

For the picoScan150 ports and the documented factory defaults, see the Cybersecurity network-services matrix.

docs.title: Detection History
docs.text:
Record and review how often each field evaluation triggered.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

Start or stop recording detections across all evaluation groups. Choose which groups and fields to include. The statistics section shows the detection count per evaluation as live bars. A link jumps to the field evaluation to adjust fields.

docs.title: Licenses
docs.text: The picoScan software packages below enable optional device functions. Activate a purchased license through the sensor's license-management workflow. The picoScan150 PRO variants (part numbers 1134610, used in the Starter Kit, and 1142273) are delivered with the native ROS 2 license (PICOSCAN ROSCONNECT) pre-installed; check the other licenses of your variant with its Product ID on sick.com.
